items.title: In AI Do We Trust? Comparing a Transformer-Based Natural Language Processing Model Against a Traditional Content Analysis Approach to Qualitative Research
items.abstract: Central to debates about the use of artificial intelligence (AI) models for qualitative research are concerns about comparability and trust in AI generated findings. The present methodological study compared findings from a transformer-based Natural Language Processing (NLP) model, BERT, against a traditional content analysis approach to qualitative research using the same text data. We examined claims that AI models generate findings that are identical or similar to traditional qualitative approaches. The study assessed three aspects of comparability between the BERT model solution and human-coded findings that included topic labeling, classification overlap, and AI replicability. Results indicated broad similarity in the semantic meaning of topic categories generated by the BERT model and themes from content analysis. There was low overlap in the classification of individual participant responses between BERT and content analysis categories, even for categories similar in semantic meaning. Running the BERT model a second time on the same input data resulted in differences in topic categories and document classification between the two approaches. Study implications and research recommendations for the use of NLP models are discussed.

items.title: Information shock: how AI demands an evolution of information science
items.abstract: Purpose This paper argues that AI authoring is prompting an Information Shock and a new information science. The shock is not a matter of increased volume and variable quality of AI-produced information. It comes as generative AI creates a new kind of author that dissolves the document, the field’s organizing unit. This forces a reconstitution of tools, literacies and identity. Design/methodology/approach The paper applies a conceptual framework drawn from the history of Information Shocks, tracing how disruptions from cuneiform to post-World War II research data forced the field to rebuild around new objects and practices. AI is analyzed against that pattern. Findings AI produces two modes of authorship: document-like objects that enter existing infrastructures, and transactional, co-authored exchanges with no stable unit to catalog, retrieve, cite or verify. The second mode renders AI literacy inadequate, even in its current forms, because they presuppose an identifiable object and human interlocutors. Anticipated changes reach professional identity, tools, intellectual property and education. Research limitations/implications The argument is theoretical and prospective, and some anticipated changes remain speculative. The Information Shock outlined is anticipated to have major impacts for librarians and information professionals moving forward. Originality/value The paper offers a historically grounded distinction between document-producing and transactional AI authorship, arguing that AI is pushing the exchange to take the mediating position that the field has long held.

items.title: Informing users about LLMs' environmental costs encourages ethical consumption
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are becoming deeply embedded in everyday human-AI interaction. However, the environmental costs associated with using those tools remain elusive. Here, we address the question of whether providing users with information about the environmental costs of using LLMs tempers their use. Such information highlights an ethical tension: acting pro-environmentally requires people to forgo some of the benefits AI tools provide. We study how people solve this trade-off in tasks that are relatively easy to tackle without using LLMs and further assess if the impact of providing such information has a stronger effect on people who have stronger environmental concerns. In two preregistered experiments (total N = 1,200), we studied participants’ use of ChatGPT in a text-editing task after they learned about the tool’s environmental costs. Results revealed that (i) raising awareness of ChatGPT’s environmental costs reduced its use and usage volume; (ii) interacting with a sycophantic model, one that encourages continuous use, did not attenuate the awareness effect, although it led to greater overall use; and (iii) raising awareness was especially effective among people with high environmental concerns. The findings highlight how raising awareness concerning LLM’s environmental costs can encourage responsible consumption.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

items.title: Inject a Turn, Not a Token: Learning Where to Redirect LLM Reasoning for Self-Correction
items.abstract: Large language models struggle to reliably identify and correct errors in their own reasoning. Unlike prior training-based approaches that fine-tune an LLM to generate revisions or feedback, we learn where to intervene in failed rollouts and determine how to redirect them. To choose where to intervene, we train a 130K-parameter MLP head on a frozen encoder using only final-answer correctness. For redirection, we find that under a fixed generation budget, the tested inline injections fail to reliably redirect reasoning, whereas presenting the same instruction in a new user turn changes the model's course. The resulting correction framework, UPTURN (User-Prompt TURN injection at a learned position), requires no LLM fine-tuning: it retains a selected prefix, injects an instruction as a new user turn, and regenerates the suffix. Across four reasoners and six math benchmarks, UPTURN improves average accuracy in every setting over a 32-rollout baseline. It outperforms self-correction and reflection-token injection baselines under matched correction budgets, transfers across reasoners and to GPQA-Diamond without retraining, and complements GRPO and self-correction methods.

items.title: Innovative Job Performance in Digitally Enabled Workplaces: A Systematic Review and Bibliometric Synthesis of Individual-Level Innovative Work Behavior
items.abstract: Innovative job performance (IJP) and innovative work behavior (IWB) are examined across distinct leadership, work-design, motivational, knowledge-sharing, and digital-work literatures. This review combines systematic full-text screening, bibliometric mapping, and a Theory–Context–Characteristics–Methodology (TCCM) synthesis to examine the individual-level evidence. The documented Scopus search of 19 September 2026 returned 23,225 records before database filters; 182 journal articles published in 2023–2026 were retained for Bibliometrix/Biblioshiny analysis. The available retrieval archive contained 90 PDF instances, including four exact duplicates. Of 86 unique full-text reports screened, 43 met the focused eligibility criteria. The 182-record bibliometric dataset covered 91 sources and 603 unique author names, with recurrent terms involving innovative work behavior, engagement, leadership, psychological empowerment, and knowledge sharing. The focused synthesis identified distinct organizational resources, motivational mechanisms, knowledge processes, and digital capabilities associated with IJP/IWB in the included studies. Much of the primary evidence relied on cross-sectional designs, and the higher-education substream was geographically concentrated. Within the bounded 182-record export, “excellencism” was absent from the searched metadata fields, and no record directly compared Generation Z and Millennials within an IJP/IWB model. The resulting conceptual framework should be interpreted as an evidence-informed synthesis rather than a causally validated model. Future research should improve temporal, multisource, multilevel, and measurement-invariant testing.

items.title: Instruction-Following LLM Agent for Simulating Human Memory Retrieval Process in Household Tasks
items.abstract: Human decision-making in dynamic household environments depends on memory retrieval processes that shape action selection and timing. This paper presents an instruction-following LLM agent as an executable human performance model for simulating memory retrieval behavior in household tasks. The proposed framework integrates memory encoding and decision-making modules with a modified ACT-R base-level activation equation that incorporates environmental entropy and observation duration. The framework was evaluated using human behavioral data from an AI2-THOR-based household task study. When predicting human search times, the modified equation produced lower prediction errors than the conventional ACT-R baseline, reducing MAE, RMSE, and MAPE by 11.08%, 5.37%, and 16.00%, respectively. These findings provide preliminary evidence that incorporating context-sensitive retrieval factors may support closer alignment with human search-time behavior in executable LLM-based human performance models.

items.title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence Into Nursing Care Planning
items.abstract: This methodological study evaluated and compared the content quality and appropriateness of nursing care plans developed by nurses and artificial intelligence (AI) for addressing the psychosocial problems of patients with stomas. Two nursing care plans addressing the psychosocial needs of a patient with a stoma were developed: 1 generated by nurses and 1 generated by an AI system. The content quality and appropriateness of the care plans were independently evaluated by 12 experts, including nursing academics and clinical nurses, using the DISCERN measurement tool. Inter-rater reliability was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). The mean DISCERN score of the nurse-generated care plan was significantly higher than that of the AI-generated care plan (P=.008). Inter-rater agreement demonstrated good agreement. The findings indicate that nurse-generated care plans demonstrate superior content quality and overall integrity compared to AI-generated plans. AI-generated care plans exhibit potential as supportive tools in nursing care planning.

items.title: Integrating generative AI with multimodal interaction to inquire into scientific phenomena
items.abstract: This study developed and evaluated two customised generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) chatbots designed to provide stepwise guidance for secondary students’ inquiry into scientific phenomena. Biology and physics chatbots were developed using the Predict–Observe–Explain (POE) framework and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to align with Singapore science syllabuses and incorporated segmented video demonstrations. 14 evaluators quantitatively and qualitatively assessed the chatbots in terms of Accuracy, Clarity, Dialogue flow, Ease of use, and Efficiency. Both chatbots were rated positively overall, particularly for Ease of use, Clarity, Efficiency, and Accuracy, while Dialogue flow received lower ratings, especially for the physics chatbot. Qualitative feedback identified needs for stronger scaffolding, better handling of follow-up questions, and additional multimodal support. items.title: Integrating generative artificial intelligence facilitates faculty interaction network and role transition in a biostatistics curriculum
items.abstract: In a two-year action-research study within an undergraduate biostatistics curriculum for nursing, pharmacy, and medical biotechnology students, we examined how generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) facilitates educators to design, supervise, and evaluate learning. Students used GenAI first as a technical tutor and then as a partner in knowledge co-creation in case-based statistical problem-solving. Teachers’ reflection records and 4697 LINE messages during the study period were analyzed using qualitative coding, GenAI-assisted semantic analysis, and social network analysis. Teachers’ roles shifted from knowledge transmitters to facilitators of critical inquiry and human–GenAI co-learning. Overall, faculty communication was dense, reciprocal, and decentralized, whereas GenAI-related discourse was more selective and centralized. GenAI-related ties were less likely to form but, once formed, strongly reciprocal and locally clustered. GenAI integration can catalyze new forms of faculty leadership through expertise sharing and collaborative problem-solving. Intentional structures for cross-disciplinary exchange and reflective faculty development are needed.

items.title: Integrating large language model-generated culturally adapted verbal suggestions into music therapy for university students: A pilot randomized exploratory study
items.abstract: Previous research has suggested that culturally mismatched interventions may cause resistance and reduce the effectiveness of music-based interventions. This pilot randomized exploratory study examined the implementation and preliminary outcomes of a music-based intervention incorporating large language model (LLM)-generated, culturally adapted verbal suggestions among Chinese undergraduate students. A total of 113 participants were randomly assigned to three multicomponent conditions: (1) Chinese film music accompanied by LLM-generated verbal suggestions involving Eastern imagery, (2) a standardized music therapy recording with conventional verbal guidance, or (3) piano music without verbal guidance. Following a 40-minute cognitively demanding task, participants completed pre- and post-intervention measures of state anxiety, positive and negative affect, and heart rate. Baseline-adjusted ANCOVAs showed no group differences in positive affect, F(2, 109) = 1.03, p = .360, ηp2 = .019, or state anxiety, F(2, 109) = 0.68, p = .511, ηp2 = .012. A significant group effect was found for negative affect, F(2, 109) = 4.60, p = .012, ηp2 = .078; the Eastern imagery group had lower adjusted post-intervention scores than both comparison groups (Holm-adjusted ps = .026). Heart rate also differed across groups, F(2, 109) = 10.56, p < .001, ηp2 = .162, with lower adjusted values in the standardized therapy group than in the other two groups. The findings identify potentially meaningful response patterns but do not establish efficacy or the independent effect of culturally adapted verbal suggestions because the conditions differed in musical material and duration. Larger, controlled trials are required. (ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT07359950).

items.title: Integrating sentiment and contextual information for suicide ideation detection in online social networks: a BERT-BiTCN-sentiment hybrid approach
items.abstract: Background Worldwide, suicide ranks as one of the primary causes of mortality. Taking action and implementing measures to address suicidal thoughts is essential for the well-being of public health. Today, methodologies developed by artificial intelligence serve important functions in the medical field, both as decision-making systems and as sources of information. This observation highlights the increasing integration of machine learning and deep learning into psychiatry, complementing traditional medical practices. Digital social platforms can significantly contribute to the early diagnosis of suicidal tendencies and the implementation of preventive measures. Individuals increasingly express their thoughts and feelings on platforms such as Twitter, Facebook, Reddit, and Instagram. It has been observed that many individuals struggling with severe psychological disorders express their feelings and reactions on social media platforms. This research aims to early detect suicidal ideation by developing a hybrid model that automatically detects suicide-related posts on online social networks (OSNs). Method First, three datasets were combined to create a new dataset of 254,198 samples. Subsequently, data preprocessing techniques were implemented to diminish the dataset’s size and mitigate noise in the data. Additionally, word embedding techniques, including Term Frequency Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF), N-Gram-TF-IDF, and Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT), were employed during the feature engineering phase. At the same time, the compound sentiment score for each post was computed for integration into the hybrid model. This study developed the BERT-Bidirectional Temporal Convolutional Network (BiTCN)-Sentiment (BERT-BiTCN-Sentiment) model by integrating BERT’s capacity to extract contextual meaning from textual data with BiTCN’s proficiency in capturing bidirectional relationships in sequential data. The BERT-BiTCN-Sentiment hybrid model proposed in this study was used for the first time to detect suicidal ideation in social networks. Results The experimental studies demonstrated that the BERT-BiTCN-Sentiment model attained superior performance, achieving an accuracy of 95.45%, precision of 95.45%, recall of 95.45%, and an F-score of 95.45%. The Multilingual BERT model achieved 94.88% accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, ranking second among the models. Moreover, the A Lite BERT (ALBERT), MentalBERT, BERT-Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM), BERT-Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), and BERT models attained comparable results. The TF-IDF-LightGBM model proved to be the most proficient among the machine learning models, attaining 90.60% in accuracy, precision, recall, and F-score. This study culminated in the development of a successful hybrid model capable of early detection of posts indicative of suicidal tendencies among users on online social networks.

items.title: Integrating technology anxiety into the TPB-TAM framework to examine AI adoption intention in hospital HRM: a study of Chinese healthcare professionals
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) can empower healthcare professionals to make data-driven decisions and streamline administrative tasks in hospital human resource management (HRM). However, it is vital to understand their perceptions towards AI for seamless implementation in practice. Therefore, the study aimed to assess the role of technology anxiety within an integrated framework combining the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) to better understand adoption intentions in this high-stakes context. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 547 healthcare professionals working in hospitals across China. Data were analyzed using structural equation modeling, including confirmatory factor analysis, path analysis, and bootstrap mediation testing. Multi-group structural equation modeling was also used to compare healthcare professionals with different levels of AI familiarity. The integrated model explained 49.4% of the variance in behavioral intention, and all twelve hypothesized paths were statistically significant. Technology anxiety was negatively associated with perceived ease of use (β = -0.553, p < 0.001), perceived behavioral control (β = -0.371, p < 0.001), attitude (β = -0.339, p < 0.001), and subjective norms (β = -0.451, p < 0.001), and it was also associated with behavioral intention through multiple indirect pathways. Multi-group analysis showed that the association between perceived ease of use and perceived usefulness was stronger among professionals with low AI familiarity, while the remaining paths remained stable across groups. AI adoption intention in hospital HRM appears to involve more than rational evaluations of usefulness and ease of use. Emotional states, such as technology anxiety, also play a role. Reducing technology anxiety and improving ease of use for users with lower AI familiarity are therefore important steps for promoting AI adoption intention. These findings highlight the value of addressing emotional factors alongside cognitive beliefs when introducing AI tools in healthcare organizations.

items.title: Integration of AI agents to promote metaverse capabilities in supply chain logistics
items.abstract: Purpose: This study is focused on capability enhancement for artificial intelligence (AI)-driven digital twins of warehouses, logistics hubs, and supply chain networks, which can be created within the metaverse. Integration of real-time data from Internet of Things (IoT) devices can update sophisticated systems which implemented new and emerging technologies, allowing for virtual monitoring, predictive maintenance, and process optimization. This study will provide insights into what capabilities can be enhanced for a seamless integration and implementation of this technology. Methodology: This is a structured literature review of 36 articles that emphasize on the capabilities that are implementing this technology and creating a more resilient ecosystem. The structured literature review would follow the PRISMA flow method to shortlist the best-fit articles for this study. Findings: The best-fit articles would be used to create a conceptual framework that would help the development of the integration of AI agents in the metaverse ecosystem and enhance the capabilities to make a resilient organization. The strategies that can help in intelligent planning and simulation would be utilized to create a competitive advantage for the firms. Conclusion: The fusion of AI agents and the metaverse marks a transformative leap in supply chain logistics, aligning with the human-centric vision of Industry 5.0. This integration not only enhances operational efficiency but also promotes a seamless collaboration between humans and intelligent systems within immersive virtual environments. Originality: The enhancement in capabilities is an essential part of the implementation of this technology. This is specifically targeted to create more resilient firms and an overall positive firm performance to survive in Industry 5.0.

items.title: Integrative Bioinformatics Analysis Incorporating Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Identifies Putative Pathogenic HNF1B Missense Variants Associated with HNF1B-MODY
items.abstract: Maturity-onset diabetes of the young type 5 (MODY5 or HNF1B-MODY) is a rare form of diabetes caused by variants in HNF1B. Patients with MODY5 exhibit high blood sugar levels and symptoms commonly associated with both type 1 and type 2 diabetes (T1D, T2D), along with kidney and pancreatic issues. Nonetheless, diagnosis, treatment and management approaches depend on specific genotype–phenotype associations. Interpretation of HNF1B missense variants remains challenging because of conflicting classifications and limited clinical evidence. This study aimed to improve the interpretation of HNF1B missense variants with conflicting evidence regarding pathogenicity and thereby advance the genetic and molecular understanding of HNF1B-MODY. An integrative computational approach combining artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and conventional bioinformatic tools, including Panther, SIFT, SNAP2, Meta-SNP, PhD-SNP, PolyPhen-2, and AlphaMissense, was used to identify deleterious missense variants in the HNF1B gene. The variants were further processed to determine their effects on protein conformation, stability, function, and conservation across species. Among 982 reported variants retrieved from the ClinVar database, 368 were classified as missense. Only 47 missense variants were labelled with conflicting classification and reported with clinical uncertainty. Consensus analysis by all tools identified five candidate variants (His153Arg, Asn298Asp, Arg303His, Lys305Glu, and Val458Gly), representing 10.6% (5/47) as potentially pathogenic. AlphaMissense classified all five as likely pathogenic, with scores ranging from 0.8921 to 1.000. Secondary structure analysis indicates that the His153Arg, Asn298Asp, Arg303His, and Lys305Glu variants are in the helical region, while the Val458Gly variant is located within the coil region. Interestingly, all five filtered variants are predicted by the I-Mutant and MuPro tools to reduce protein stability. The three-dimensional (3D) protein structures were constructed using the Deep Learning-Based Iterative Threading Assembly Refinement (D-I-TASSER) tool and visualised by UCSF Chimera. Structural modelling showed similarity between the mutant and wild-type models, with RMSD values ranging from 0.77 to 1.36 Å. The multiple sequence alignments show that amino acids at variant sites across all variants are highly conserved among species. These findings show that combining traditional bioinformatics with artificial intelligence and machine learning improves the interpretation of HNF1B missense variants with clinical uncertainty. Integrating computational predictions with structural, evolutionary, and clinical data provides a framework for prioritising variants for further functional and clinical investigation.

items.title: Intelligent Circuit Design: Exploring Artificial Intelligence for Logic Gate Synthesis and Optimization
items.abstract: Modern integrated circuits contain billions of logic gates, while thermal and sub-micron parasitic limits make every design decision more expensive. Classical logic synthesis relies on deterministic minimization and hand-engineered heuristics that struggle to balance Power, Performance, and Area (PPA) at the same time. This paper reviews how Artificial Intelligence (AI) can support logic gate synthesis in Electronic Design Automation (EDA): Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for circuit representation and early PPA prediction, Reinforcement Learning (RL) for restructuring And-Inverter Graphs (AIGs) and Majority-Inverter Graphs (MIGs), and Transformer-based Large Circuit Models (LCMs) and Large Language Models (LLMs) for hardware generation. Building on the survey of Astillero (2026), it proposes a verification-first hybrid framework in which learned models suggest optimizations and formal equivalence checking guarantees correctness, together with an experimental protocol for evaluating it against classical flows.

items.title: Intelligent Robots for Elderly Care: Categories, Application Scenarios, and Challenges
items.abstract: Aging populations have increased the demand for intelligent, personalized, and emotionally supportive elderly care services. Traditional care models often face limitations such as high labor costs, insufficient service continuity, and limited emotional support. Deep learning-driven elderly care robots provide a promising solution by integrating perception, decision-making, human-robot interaction, and adaptive service functions. This paper reviews the major categories of intelligent elderly care robots, including rehabilitation robots, nursing robots, and companion robots. It further discusses their application scenarios in home care, nursing homes, and community-based care. Existing studies show that deep learning, machine vision, multimodal sensing, and large language models can improve motion assistance, health monitoring, emotional interaction, and personalized companionship. However, several challenges remain, including technical reliability, data privacy, ethical risks, high deployment costs, and user acceptance among older adults. Future development should focus on lightweight models, multimodal fusion, privacy-preserving learning, and human-centered design. Intelligent elderly care robots should not replace human caregivers, but should support them in providing safer, more efficient, and more compassionate care.

items.title: Intelligent Technologies as Proponents of Global Development and Sustainability: An Approach Based on India's Digital Infrastructure
items.abstract: The seventeen core goals of the UN's 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development demand the need for collective action along social, economic, and environmental fronts. Artificial intelligence (AI), the Internet of Things (IoT), blockchain, along with cloud/edge computing are notable examples of intelligent technologies and also regarded as facilitators of this agenda. However, the literature that discusses these technologies tends to interpret technology and policy goals in isolation, thus paying inconsistent attention across the seventeen goals and hardly establishing its claims on the realities of any one nation. This paper aims to bridge that gap. It presents a taxonomy of intelligent technologies, aligns them onto a particular segment of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) involving infrastructure, human well-being, education, energy and climate, disparities, and sustainable cities, and foundations that connecting on case studies from smart city initiatives and digital public infrastructure projects in India. With the goal to lead future technology-for-development research, the research study builds on this depiction and recommends a four-layer conceptual framework: Infrastructure, Intelligence, Trust, and Impact. It draws its conclusion by inspecting the obstacles that challenge this optimism, such as the digital gap, data privacy, a bias in the algorithm and environmental impact of computation itself, before emphasizing federated and privacy-preserving techniques as a feasible direction for further research. Keywords: artificial intelligence; federated learning; smart cities; Internet of things; Sustainable Development Goals; Digital Public Infrastructure

items.title: Interpersonal Competence as a Dimension of Global Competence and its Relationship with Academic Motivation among Undergraduate Students
items.abstract: Global competence is integral to higher education because students need the knowledge, skills, and attitudes to learn effectively and participate in an interconnected world. Interpersonal competence is one part of it: the ability to cooperate and communicate with people from different cultural and educational backgrounds. This study examined the relationship between interpersonal competence (Skills) and undergraduate students' academic motivation, using a quantitative correlational design. Data were collected from 1,200 undergraduate students in the Education departments of three universities in Lahore. The Skills dimension of the Global Competence Scale (Liu et al., 2020) measured interpersonal competence, and the Academic Motivation Scale (AMS) measured academic motivation. Pearson product-moment correlations were computed between skills and intrinsic motivation, extrinsic motivation, and amotivation. Skills showed statistically significant moderate positive correlations with intrinsic motivation (r = 0.409, p < 0.001) and extrinsic motivation (r = 0.364, p < .001), and a statistically significant but very weak negative correlation with amotivation (r = −0.133, p < 0.001). Students with stronger interpersonal skills therefore tended to report higher intrinsic and extrinsic motivation, while the association with amotivation was small.

items.title: Interpersonal Emotion Regulation in Middle Childhood: From Cognitive Capacity to Context-Sensitive Regulation
items.abstract: Interpersonal emotion regulation (IER) requires individuals to understand another person’s emotional state and adapt regulatory decisions to interpersonal goals and situational demands. Across four linked studies, the present research examined age-related patterns, cognitive and social-cognitive correlates, contextual modulation, and individual differences in context sensitivity in children aged 8–10 years. IER was assessed using vignette-based strategy ratings, executive-function and social-cognitive measures, and experimental manipulations of regulatory goals and demands. Across the observed age range, increasing age was associated with greater cognitive and affective engagement and lower avoidance and co-rumination, whereas distraction and suppression showed no significant age associations. Executive function, empathy, and theory of mind were systematically associated with greater adaptive and lower maladaptive IER. Children also altered their regulatory decisions as social goals and regulatory demands changed. Person-by-context analyses showed selective effects: general cognitive-control capacity moderated responsiveness to regulatory goals, whereas social cognition moderated demand-related variation in cognitive engagement. Together, the findings suggest that IER in middle childhood involves not only developing regulatory capacities but also coordinating those capacities with the goals and demands of interpersonal situations.

items.title: Interpreting Machine Learning Predictions with SHAP and LIME for Transparent Decision Making
items.abstract: Machine learning models increasingly influence critical decisions across diverse domains, yet their complex architectures often operate as black boxes, obscuring the rationale behind predictions and limiting stakeholder trust. This research demonstrates a comprehensive, reproducible workflow for applying explainable artificial intelligence techniques to interpret Random Forest classifier decisions using publicly available data and standard computational resources. The study implements and compares two leading explanation methods, SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) and LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations), on the Titanic survival prediction task to evaluate their consistency and practical utility. The methodology encompasses automated data preprocessing, model training with regularization to prevent overfitting, and systematic generation of both global and local explanations through multiple visualization formats. Results reveal exceptional agreement between explanation methods, with Spearman rank correlation of 0.918 and Pearson correlation of 0.982 for feature importance values. Both techniques consistently identified passenger sex as the dominant predictive feature, contributing approximately 15.4% and 12.5% of model decisions respectively, followed by passenger class and fare. The Random Forest model achieved 84.5% test set ROC-AUC with controlled overfitting (0.040 ROC-AUC gap between training and test sets) while maintaining interpretable complexity through architectural constraints. The implementation executes efficiently on CPU hardware within minutes, eliminating computational barriers to XAI adoption. This work establishes that current explainability techniques can provide reliable, consistent insights into ensemble model decisions while remaining accessible to researchers and practitioners with limited computational resources.

items.title: Intuitive Robot Programming
items.abstract: The introduction of robots in SMEs requires a drastic reconsideration of existing programming techniques and interfaces. The growing versatility of the market essentially demands the robots to be re-programmed frequently, calling for interfaces that are intuitive enough to require no robotic expertise, yet flexible enough to meet industrial needs. Rather than limiting the intervention of the workers, the technology should empower them to take control over the machine. Only then, the human-machine complementarity can be leveraged, combining the efficiency of automation with the flexibility of human work. Ergonomics and human factors are critical to the development of these new programming interfaces, which should typically be developed and tested in a cyclic fashion with the end-users. In this chapter, we highlight the differences between easy-to-learn and easy-to-use interfaces, as well as the differences between interfaces targeting naive/casual users and interfaces targeting expert/professional workers. We discuss the design of robot programming interfaces based on a user-centric perspective. The research developments in this project target different methods to collect demonstrations (including tracked devices and kinesthetic teaching), different graphical user interfaces (including block-based and timeline representations), and different approaches to augmented reality (including tablets/smartphones, headsets or actuated projection devices). Through this multi-modular approach, we aim at providing workers with the most natural way possible to interact with the robot depending on the task or their preferences.

items.title: Job Demands and Resources in Personnel Assessment Consulting from the Perspective of Perceived Cognitive Workload
items.abstract: Johdanto: Tietotyö asettaa paljon samanaikaisia vaatimuksia työntekijän tiedonkäsittelylle. Henkilöarviointi on yksi suosiotaan kasvattanut tietotyö, jota käytetään yhtenä osana työntekijöiden rekrytointiprosessia. Useimmiten henkilöarviointi tuotetaan konsultointityönä. Itse henkilöarviointi vaatii arvioinnin tekijältä paljon tiedon syvällistä prosessointia ja konsultointityön luonne vaatii nopeaa reagointia. Korkea kognitiivinen työkuorma (cognitive workload) voi heikentää työntekijän työhyvinvointia ja työssä suoriutumista, joten on tärkeää tutkia, mitkä tekijät liittyvät kognitiivisen työkuorman kokemukseen. Työn resurssien ja vaatimusten mallin (job demands-resources model, JD-R) mukaisesti vaatimusten lisäksi työn resurssit vaikuttavat työn kuormittavuuteen. Tässä maisterintutkielmassa pyrittiin selvittämään kognitiivisen työkuorman kokemukseen liittyviä vaatimuksia ja resursseja henkilöarviointikonsulttien työssä. Menetelmä: Tutkimukseen osallistui yhdeksän konsulttia, joista kaikille toteutettiin puolistrukturoitu haastattelu. Haastattelut toteutettiin kasvotusten tai Zoom-videoviestintäpalvelussa. Kaikki haastattelut litteroitiin, ja aineisto analysoitiin teoriaohjaavasti temaattisen analyysin menetelmin. Tulokset: Analyysin myötä muodostetut teemat jaettiin JD-R mallin mukaisesti vaatimuksiin ja resursseihin. Vaatimuksista muodostettiin neljä pääteemaa: tulokselliset vaatimukset, kognitiiviset vaatimukset, sisäsyntyiset vaatimukset, sekä häiriötekijät. Resursseista muodostettiin kolme pääteemaa: kognitiivisen prosessoinnin tukeminen, optimaaliset olosuhteet, sekä positiiviset kokemukset. Pohdinta: Haastateltavat toivat esiin enemmän vaatimuksia kuin resurssitekijöitä. Kaiken kaikkiaan tulokset osoittivat, että henkilöarviointikonsultointityössä on paljon vaatimuksia, ja vaatimukset ovat usein korkeita. Tulokset osoittivat myös, että henkilöarviointikonsultointityössä resurssit ovat lähinnä työskentelyä tukevia tekijöitä eivätkä kuormitusta kompensoivia tekijöitä. Tutkimus auttaa ymmärtämään tietotyön kognitiiviseen työkuorman kokemukseen liittyvien tekijöiden laaja-alaisuutta. Tulokset auttavat myös ymmärtämään, mihin asioihin henkilöarviointityössä tulisi puuttua kognitiivisen työkuorman kokemuksen optimoimiseksi. Tämän tutkimuksen tulosten pohjalta henkilöarviointikonsultointityöhön vaikuttavia vaatimuksia ja resursseja voidaan tutkia seuraavaksi määrällisesti.

items.title: Keep or wave? Evaluating static and dynamic gestures across in-vehicle function-control tasks
items.abstract: Mid-air gesture interaction is a promising input modality for in-vehicle information systems, but the relative suitability of static and dynamic gestures across vehicle functions remains unclear. Thirty-three licenced drivers completed a within-subject driving-simulator experiment involving nine in-vehicle function-control tasks. Vehicle-control stability, hand-off-wheel duration, gesture-execution fidelity, and subjective user experience were assessed, and linear mixed-effects models examined gesture type, task, and their interaction. Gesture type did not significantly affect longitudinal- or lateral-control stability. However, static gestures produced shorter hand-off-wheel durations, higher execution fidelity, and more favourable ratings of perceived validity, satisfaction, perceived safety, and learnability. Significant gesture type × task interactions emerged for interaction performance and all user-experience dimensions. Static gestures performed relatively consistently across tasks, whereas dynamic gestures were more task dependent. These findings suggest that the evaluated static gestures may serve as more robust candidates, whereas dynamic gestures should be selected according to task-specific gesture-command compatibility.

items.title: Kognitive Mobilität unter KI-Bedingungen - Professionelle Denkarbeit in dauerhafter Mensch-KI-Kooperation
items.abstract: Der vorliegende Text entwickelt das Modell der Kognitiven Mobilität (Cognitive Mobility) als Versuch, professionelle Denkarbeit unter Bedingungen dauerhafter KI-Mitwirkung zu beschreiben. Ausgangspunkt ist nicht die Frage, ob KI grundsätzlich Arbeit schneller macht, sondern wie sie die Bedingungen verändert, unter denen professionelles Denken entsteht, sich bewegt und sich selbst überprüft. Im Zentrum steht die Annahme, dass KI nicht angemessen als bloßes Werkzeug zur Entlastung beschrieben werden kann. Sie verändert die Verteilung kognitiver Last und damit die Bedingungen professioneller Denkarbeit. KI kann den Zugang zu komplexen Denkoperationen erleichtern, Material erschließen, Perspektiven öffnen und professionelle Handlungsmöglichkeiten erweitern. Zugleich erzeugt genau diese Erleichterung ein neues Risiko: Wenn der Zugang zum Denken friktionsärmer wird, kann auch der Unterschied zwischen eigener Urteilsbildung und maschinell erzeugter Anschlussfähigkeit verwischen. Diesen gerichteten Zug KI-gestützter Arbeitsumgebungen zur Reduktion kognitiver Reibung fasst das Modell als Cognitive Gravity — seinen zentralen Risikobegriff: Man nutzt KI nicht einfach; man bewegt sich in einem Feld, das eine Richtung hat. Das Modell unterscheidet vier Modi der Mensch-KI-Kooperation: Cognitive Relief, Cognitive Offloading, Cognitive Augmentation und Cognitive Transformation. Sie sind keine Aufstiegsstufen, sondern funktionale Formen kognitiver Lastverteilung, die produktiv sein, aber auch kippen können. Quer zu diesen Modi steht Cognitive Recognition als Querschnittskompetenz: die Fähigkeit, KI-generierte Muster kritisch zu lesen. Zentrale Voraussetzung produktiver KI-Nutzung ist Cognitive Loading: der eigenständige Aufbau fachlicher, sprachlicher und epistemischer Strukturen, bevor diese durch KI entlastet oder erweitert werden. Ohne dieses Loading droht eine Verschiebung vom Werkzeug zum Denkersatz. Cognitive Gravity kann dabei Cognitive Atrophy begünstigen: die Verkümmerung kognitiver Fähigkeiten durch Auslagerung vor dem Aufbau eigener Strukturen. Drift und Sedation werden als Mechanismen verstanden, über die Atrophy schleichend entsteht. Mit geliehener Souveränität beschreibt der Beitrag zudem eine Wirkung von Cognitive Gravity auf Selbstbild und Auftreten: die Diskrepanz zwischen Auftrittsgewissheit und epistemischer Deckung. Empirisch anschlussfähig ist diese Perspektive an Hoffmann et al. (2026). In einer Befragung von 4.048 Studierenden zum akademischen Schreiben mit KI wird sichtbar, dass produktive Nutzung und wahrgenommene Gefährdung eigener Denkprozesse nebeneinander bestehen: Die Autoren dokumentieren weit verbreitete KI-Nutzung, die Delegation zentraler Schreib- und Lesehandlungen sowie Bedenken, kritisches Denken zu verlernen. Besondere Bedeutung erhält ihr Hinweis auf einen möglichen „Kipp-Punkt": Wenn Studierende ihre ersten akademischen Texte bereits mit KI verfassen, kann das Gespür dafür fehlen, was ihnen durch ausgeprägte Delegation verloren geht. Cognitive Loading wird damit nicht nur zur Voraussetzung produktiver KI-Nutzung, sondern zu einer Bildungsaufgabe unter Bedingungen von Anfang an verfügbarem Cognitive Offloading. Das Modell positioniert KI als kognitives Exoskelett. Ein Exoskelett ersetzt den Körper nicht; es stützt, stabilisiert und erweitert ihn. Genau deshalb stellt sich die Frage, welche kognitiven Muskeln weiterhin belastet werden müssen, damit Unterstützung nicht in Abhängigkeit umschlägt. Das Exoskelett trägt nicht nur — es zieht auch. Kognitive Mobilität ist deshalb nicht die Abwesenheit von Cognitive Gravity, sondern die Fähigkeit, sich unter ihrer Wirkung epistemisch selbstbestimmt zu bewegen. English Abstract This working paper develops the model of Cognitive Mobility as an attempt to describe professional cognition under conditions of sustained human-AI cooperation. Its starting point is not whether AI simply makes work faster, but how it changes the conditions under which professional thinking emerges, moves, and examines itself. At the centre of the model is the assumption that AI cannot adequately be described as a mere tool of relief. It changes the distribution of cognitive load and, with it, the conditions of professional cognition. AI can facilitate access to complex cognitive operations, open up material, generate perspectives, and expand professional agency. At the same time, precisely this facilitation creates a new risk: as access to thinking becomes less frictional, the distinction between one's own judgement and machine-generated connective plausibility can begin to blur. The model names this directed pull of AI-supported working environments toward the reduction of cognitive friction Cognitive Gravity — its central risk concept: one does not simply use AI; one moves in a field that has a direction. The model distinguishes four modes of human-AI cooperation: Cognitive Relief, Cognitive Offloading, Cognitive Augmentation, and Cognitive Transformation. These are not stages of progress, but functional forms of cognitive load distribution that can be productive, yet can also tip into risk. Across these modes, Cognitive Recognition functions as a transversal competence: the ability to read AI-generated patterns critically. A central prerequisite for productive AI use is Cognitive Loading: the independent development of subject-specific, linguistic, and epistemic structures before these are relieved or extended by AI. Without such loading, AI risks shifting from tool to substitute structure. Cognitive Gravity can foster Cognitive Atrophy: the weakening or non-development of cognitive abilities through outsourcing before one's own structures have been built. Drift and Sedation are understood as mechanisms through which Atrophy can emerge gradually. With borrowed sovereignty, the paper further describes an effect of Cognitive Gravity on self-image and demeanour: the discrepancy between the confidence of one's appearance and its epistemic coverage. Empirically, this perspective resonates with Hoffmann et al. (2026). Their survey of 4,048 students on academic writing with AI shows that productive use and perceived risks to one's own thinking processes coexist. The authors document widespread AI use, the delegation of central writing and reading operations, and concerns about unlearning critical thinking. Their reference to a possible "tipping point" is particularly significant: if students write their first academic texts already with AI, they may lack a sense of what is lost through extensive delegation. Cognitive Loading thus becomes not only a prerequisite for productive AI use, but an educational task under conditions in which Cognitive Offloading is available from the outset. The model conceptualizes AI as a cognitive exoskeleton. An exoskeleton does not replace the body; it supports, stabilizes, and extends it. Precisely for this reason, the question arises which cognitive muscles must continue to be exercised so that support does not turn into dependency. The exoskeleton does not only carry — it also pulls. Cognitive Mobility is therefore not the absence of Cognitive Gravity, but the ability to move in an epistemically self-determined way under its pull.

items.title: LAND ALLOCATION USING MODERN GEODESIC EQUIPMENT: EXPERIENCE, PROBLEMS, AND PROSPECTS
items.abstract: The article is devoted to the study of the process of land plot allocation using modern geodetic equipment. The relevance of the topic is due to the fact that errors made during allocation lead to inaccuracies in the actual boundaries, area and status of the plot, cause overlapping of plots, litigation and problems with land development and construction. The study examines the regulatory framework governing the allocation procedure in the Russian Federation, considers traditional and modern technologies, and describes the methodology of geodetic works using GNSS equipment. Using the example of a land plot with cadastral number 14:35:211001:3291, located on the Vilyuysky tract in the urban district "City of Yakutsk", the boundaries were set out using two GNSS receivers EFT M4 in RTK mode with reference to the point "Pakhay2" in the MSK-14 coordinate system. Typical errors are identified: violation of gas pipeline protection zones, registry errors, errors related to the human factor, multipath and GPS spoofing. It is established that traditional methods using an optical total station require line of sight, the work of a two-person crew and are subject to instrumental and human errors, whereas GNSS receivers and robotic total stations provide centimeter accuracy and high productivity. For areas with a low density of geodetic networks, the PPK method with post-processing of data is effective. It is concluded that it is necessary to integrate modern geodetic technologies, carefully verify source data and strictly comply with regulatory requirements in order to minimize allocation errors.

items.title: Large Language Models as a Clinical Interface for Predictive Modeling: A Feasibility Study in Pediatric Appendicitis
items.abstract: Purpose Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in clinical data workflows, but most clinicians lack the time, training, or support to build predictive models. We evaluated whether a ChatGPT-assisted workflow could enable clinicians to independently construct and execute a basic predictive model using routine perioperative data, using postoperative length of stay (LOS) in pediatric appendicitis as a feasibility use case. Methods We conducted a retrospective study of 228 children undergoing laparoscopic appendectomy. Ten routinely available preoperative variables were used. ChatGPT guided preprocessing and generated code for linear regression and random forest models using naïve and structured prompting. Models were trained using an 80/20 split and evaluated using MAE, RMSE, r, and R 2 . Results Naïve prompting performed poorly, while structured prompting improved model performance (MAE 0.34, RMSE 0.85, r 0.85). On the test set, linear regression achieved MAE 1.00 and random forest 0.77. Identified variables reflected expected clinical patterns. These findings demonstrate internal consistency of the workflow rather than new predictive insight. Conclusions A structured ChatGPT workflow enabled clinicians to construct standard predictive models using routine data. These findings support feasibility of clinician-directed model development, but not clinical utility, of LLM-enabled workflows.

items.title: Large language models as sources of diabetic retinopathy patient education: a comparative evaluation of safety, health information quality, and readability
items.abstract: Background Patients increasingly use large language models (LLMs) to seek medical information, but their performance in answering diabetic retinopathy (DR) questions remains insufficiently characterized. Objective To evaluate the safety, accuracy, patient-centered communication, information quality, transparency, and readability of diabetic retinopathy information generated by widely accessible large language models. Methods Fifty standardized DR patient questions were submitted to ChatGPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, Doubao, Copilot, and Perplexity. Responses were independently evaluated by five raters using guideline-based reference answer elements. Rater-based outcomes included Safety, Accuracy, Empathy, DISCERN, EQIP, JAMA benchmark criteria, and Global Quality Score (GQS). Readability was assessed using the Automated Readability Index, Coleman–Liau Index, Flesch–Kincaid Grade Level, Gunning Fog Index, SMOG, and Flesch Reading Ease Score. Inter-rater agreement and between-model differences were analyzed using appropriate agreement statistics and paired nonparametric tests. Results Inter-rater agreement was moderate for Safety (Fleiss’ κ = 0.581) and good for non-binary outcomes, with ICC (2,1) values ranging from 0.806 to 0.870. Most responses were classified as safe, with safe response rates ranging from 86.0 to 94.0%, and no significant between-model difference was observed. Accuracy scores were generally high across models, although between-model differences were statistically significant with a small effect size. Empathy varied more noticeably, with Copilot scoring highest and Doubao and Perplexity scoring lower. Perplexity achieved the highest DISCERN and JAMA scores, while Copilot performed best on EQIP. GQS differences were small. Readability differed significantly across models, with Gemini generally producing the most readable responses; however, all models exceeded the recommended sixth-grade reading level, and all Flesch Reading Ease Scores were below the recommended threshold. Conclusion No single LLM performed best across all domains. Although the evaluated models generally provided safe and accurate responses to DR patient questions, limitations remained in safety escalation, empathy, transparency, and readability. LLM-generated DR information may support general patient education but should not replace professional ophthalmic consultation.

items.title: Leadership, burnout, and organizational mental health: a neuroscience-informed perspective
items.abstract: This article argues that the persistent burden of burnout reflects a fundamental conceptual problem—burnout continues to be framed primarily as an individual condition rather than as an occupational phenomenon shaped by interacting structural, organizational, and leadership conditions. Burnout has emerged as a major occupational health challenge. In a 2024 survey across eight predominantly high and upper-middle-income countries, 48% of respondents reported currently grappling with burnout. Separately, depression and anxiety cost the global economy approximately one trillion dollars annually in lost productivity. Drawing on evidence from neuroimaging, stress biology, cognitive neuroscience, and organizational research, this article examines plausible pathways through which leadership behavior may influence conditions that contribute to or protect against burnout, including social threat–reward processing, cognitive flexibility, emotional intelligence, psychological safety, emotional contagion, and stress-related neurobiological responses. Among physicians, burnout has been associated with depression and anxiety, while evidence regarding substance abuse is less consistent. These proposed mechanisms are proximal and potentially modifiable, but operate within broader structural conditions that constrain or enable their effects. Human-centered work design and neuroleadership-informed leadership practices are proposed as complements to broader structural interventions, with implications for health systems, workforce sustainability, and policy design.

items.title: Learning attention-enhanced relation-sensitive knowledge graph embeddings with variable receptive fields for link prediction
items.abstract: Knowledge graph embedding aims to predict missing links by learning representations of entities and relations. However, existing methods often struggle to effectively capture interaction features at multiple scales and to suppress redundant information among these multi-scale features, which hinders the model’s ability to focus on essential semantics. They also neglect the sensitivity of entities under specific relations, resulting in the lack of discriminability of entity representations. To tackle these problems, we propose a novel A ttention-enhanced R elation-sensitive V ariable receptive field-aware knowledge graph E mbedding method ( ARVE ). In this study, ARVE adopts a hybrid multi-scale grouped convolution module that extends the receptive fields of kernels in different forms to capture interaction features at multiple scales. Subsequently, ARVE introduces a feature points–convolutional kernels joint selection mechanism, which adaptively assigns weights to both convolutional kernels and specific feature locations, optimizing the adaptive fusion process of the aforementioned multi-scale features. Furthermore, a global attention block is employed to produce relation-sensitive entity representations by computing relevance scores between them, while modeling global dependencies. Experimental outcomes demonstrate that ARVE possesses a remarkable capability to capture information from local to global. It achieves notable performance across several benchmarks. In particular, on FB15k-237, ARVE improves MRR by 15.5% compared with the strongest graph neural network-based baseline DGATCL and by 6.6% compared with the overall strongest LLM-based baseline GLTW. Our code is available at https://github.com/JasmineMina07/ARVE .

items.title: Learning Beyond the Classroom: Examining Achievement and Engagement in Blended Learning Environments
items.abstract: Blended learning, which integrates face-to-face instruction with technology-mediated online components, has gained prominence as schools seek flexible and learner-centred pedagogies. This study examined the effect of a blended learning approach on the academic achievement and classroom engagement of secondary school students in Kerala, India. A quasi-experimental, non-equivalent control group design was employed with 120 ninth-grade students drawn from two comparable government-aided schools. The experimental group (n = 60) received eight weeks of blended instruction combining classroom teaching with a learning management system, interactive video lessons, and online formative quizzes, while the control group (n = 60) received conventional lecture-based instruction. Academic achievement was measured using a validated 40-item subject achievement test administered as pre-test and post-test, and engagement was assessed with a 20-item student engagement scale measuring behavioural, emotional, and cognitive dimensions. Analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), controlling for pre-test scores, revealed a statistically significant difference in post-test achievement favouring the experimental group (F = 28.64, p < .001), with a large effect size (partial eta squared = .20). The blended learning group also reported significantly higher engagement across all three dimensions, with the largest gain in cognitive engagement. Findings suggest that a well-structured blended approach can enhance both learning outcomes and engagement at the secondary level. The study recommends sustained teacher training in blended pedagogy and improved digital infrastructure, and discusses implications for classroom practice, curriculum design, and education policy.

items.title: Learning Features, Not Layouts: Feature-Axis Attention as a Transfer Prior for Medical Imaging
items.abstract: Natural-image-pretrained foundation models are increasingly adapted to medical imaging, yet transfer remains unreliable under domain shift, modality heterogeneity, and label scarcity. We trace part of this fragility to an overlooked design choice. Standard vision transformers place all global modeling on self-attention over spatial tokens, an object-layout prior well suited to natural scenes but not to medical images, where the discriminative signal lies in feature correlations and texture that recur across scanners while layout does not. We ask whether the axis of global attention, spatial versus feature, is itself a lever for transferable medical representations. Existing channel-aware hybrids confound this question, adding channel attention to a spatially-mixed backbone and leaving the axes coupled and the feature axis unmeasurable in isolation. We design FAD-ViT, a backbone that strictly decouples the two axes, making feature-axis attention the primary global operator and the attention axis a controlled variable. Evaluating comprehensively across 23 classification, segmentation, and low-data tasks under matched tokenization, capacity, and protocol, we find that shifting global attention from the spatial to the feature axis leaves from-scratch performance essentially unchanged, yet markedly strengthens transfer. Identical ImageNet pretraining yields up to roughly three times the transfer gain, with consistent improvements on every held-out segmentation task at up to a quarter the parameter count and far lower compute than standard and channel-attention baselines. The advantage is largest where texture rather than geometry is discriminative, tracking greater reuse of pretrained features. The axis of global attention is thus a design lever for medical transfer, and making it channel-primary is a simple, cheap, and principled choice.

items.title: Learning More by Training Less: Uncertainty-Guided Progressive Contraction for Efficient Reasoning Post-Training
items.abstract: Large language models have achieved remarkable advances in complex reasoning. However, scaling reasoning post-training with ever-larger corpora can substantially increase training cost without proportional performance gains. In this study, we therefore ask: how far can reasoning supervision be compressed without sacrificing capability? To this end, we propose an uncertainty-guided progressive contraction framework that concentrates supervision and optimization on the reasoning trajectories most valuable for learning. Specifically, rather than treating a teacher-generated chain-of-thought (CoT) as a single realized path, we construct uncertainty-profiled reasoning supervision by building Monte Carlo reasoning trees around intermediate reasoning states to expose process-level uncertainty. This uncertainty first contracts the original corpus into a compact teacher-informed pool. A second, learner-aware contraction then performs online routing during SFT, concentrating optimization according to the student's evolving learning state. Together, the two stages progressively contract both supervision and optimization, substantially reducing the student training budget. Experiments across diverse reasoning benchmarks and LLM families show that our method uses as little as 0.22% of the optimization budget of full-data SFT, over 450x less training exposure, while maintaining or improving reasoning performance. Notably, our framework generalizes well across heterogeneous student families, black-box teachers, and weak-to-strong transfer. This indicates that it is not only a way to accelerate training but can also enhance reasoning capability.

items.title: Learning to Distrust Correct Answers: The Effect of Deliberate AI-Induced Ambiguity on Conceptual Reasoning in Electrical Engineering Students
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is rapidly becoming part of engineering students’ learning environments, particularly in quantitative problem solving, explanation generation, and formative feedback. The educational value of these systems, however, depends not only on output accuracy but also on whether learners can evaluate claims that appear authoritative. This paper proposes Deliberate Ambiguity Verification (DAV), an instructional framework in which electrical engineering students compare two AI-generated solutions that are mathematically plausible and professionally presented but differ in a consequential assumption, boundary condition, or physical interpretation. Students must identify the point of divergence, verify each response against an independent engineering principle, justify a decision, and report confidence before and after verification. The framework integrates epistemic vigilance, trust calibration, metacognitive monitoring, cognitive engagement, productive failure, and discipline-specific AI literacy. A randomized four-condition design is proposed for students in circuit analysis, contrasting no-AI problem solving, a single AI answer, a plausible-but-incorrect AI answer, and deliberate ambiguity. Primary outcomes are conceptual reasoning, verification behavior, confidence calibration, and AI-free transfer. The paper argues that the goal should not be generalized distrust of AI, but calibrated skepticism: the capacity to determine when an AI response should be accepted provisionally, when it requires independent verification, and when disciplinary reasoning should override the apparent authority of the system. The framework is intended to provide a testable pathway for studying epistemically responsible human-AI collaboration in engineering education.

items.title: Legal Chameleons: Political Ideology, Institutional Histories, and Firms’ Management of Identity Cues
items.abstract: This study examines how foreign firms strategically manage the salience of foreignness when facing unfavorable domestic evaluators. Foreign firms do so by altering the ethnic composition of the agents representing them before the evaluators. We examine this question in the context of Asian firms’ selection of legal counsel in U.S. federal courts. Prior research suggests that foreign firms may anticipate less favorable evaluations in courts that have historically favored domestic over foreign firms and in those with conservative judges. We argue that, in such evaluative settings, Asian firms adjust the ethnic composition of their external legal teams to manage the salience of foreignness, and that such adjustments are especially likely in courts that combine judge conservatism with pro-domestic ruling histories. We test these arguments using data on U.S. patent litigation from 2000 to 2016 and validated measures of courts’ political ideology and pro-domestic ruling histories. We find that Asian firms reduce the proportion of Asian-origin lawyers and increase the proportion of White lawyers when litigating in conservative courts, particularly when these courts also have pro-domestic ruling histories. By contrast, the ethnic composition of lawyers representing domestic firms remains stable across courts. Evidence of implicit bias against Asians among legal professionals provides additional support consistent with the theorized mechanism. Post-hoc analyses reveal that adjusting the ethnic composition of external legal teams attenuates the likelihood of unfavorable outcomes in conservative courts. These findings contribute to research on liability of foreignness by identifying agent selection as a specific mitigation mechanism in evaluative arenas.

items.title: Leveraging Architectural Diversity for DNA Sequence Classification
items.abstract: The rapid evolution of high-throughput sequencing technologies has effectively transformed DNA sequencers into advanced genomic biosensors. However, the accurate functional annotation and classification of raw DNA sequences directly from these biosensor outputs, without manual feature extraction, remain central challenges in computational genomics. While deep learning methods have shown remarkable success in specialized tasks, such as viral genome detection in complex sensor-derived biological samples, a comprehensive evaluation of how diverse architectural paradigms generalize across varied genomic sensing contexts warrants further investigation. In this study, we extend beyond domain-specific models by benchmarking a broad spectrum of deep learning architectures, ranging from pure Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and self-attention mechanisms to hybrid CNN-Transformer frameworks and pre-trained genomic foundation models (DNABERT-2) augmented with motif-refinement modules; moreover, we propose a novel hybrid CNN-Transformer architecture. Furthermore, we develop a comprehensive ensemble strategy that integrates these diverse architectures while systematically varying key training hyperparameters, including data augmentation techniques and loss functions, to optimize predictive performance. We evaluate models across a diverse suite of genomic datasets, encompassing viral host classification, Escherichia coli promoter recognition, and human enhancer classification. Our comparative analysis highlights the relative trade-offs between convolutional local feature extraction and attention-based global context modeling when processing high-dimensional sequence data acquired by genomic sensors. The results demonstrate that ensemble and attention-guided models consistently achieve superior generalization and robustness across distinct genomic classification tasks, providing a systematic framework for robust computational analysis of sequencing derived DNA sequences.

items.title: Lightweight Time-Frequency Vibration Sensing for Consumer Device Condition Monitoring
items.abstract: Consumer rotating devices, including washing machines, air conditioners, electric fans, robotic vacuum cleaners, and home fitness equipment, increasingly rely on vibration sensing for intelligent condition monitoring and predictive maintenance. Ensuring reliable operation in these resource-constrained appliances requires efficient, lightweight artificial intelligence (AI) solutions capable of processing non-stationary signals under real-world operational interference. This paper proposes a lightweight AI-assisted vibration sensing framework that employs continuous wavelet transform (CWT) and Hilbert-Huang transform (HHT) to convert one-dimensional (1-D) vibration time-series signals into two-dimensional (2-D) time-frequency representations. These representations are subsequently analyzed using lightweight deep learning architectures, specifically MobileNetV3-Small, ConvNeXt-Tiny, and the You Only Look Once version 11 classification model (YOLOv11-cls). Public bearing benchmark datasets, including Case Western Reserve University (CWRU), Paderborn University (PU), and Intelligent Maintenance Systems (IMS), are utilized as representative rotating components to investigate model generalization. The proposed framework is designed with eventual embedded deployment in consumer electronics in mind. Experimental results demonstrate that CWT combined with YOLOv11-cls achieves high diagnostic accuracy, while MobileNetV3-Small provides an attractive low-latency alternative for computationally constrained edge platforms. Conventional random splitting is also compared with dataset-specific structured isolation. The results highlight the importance of avoiding data leakage and quantify tradeoffs in classification accuracy, parameter count, floating-point operations (FLOPs), model footprint, preprocessing cost, and central processing unit (CPU) inference latency.

items.title: LINGUOCULTURAL CHARACTERISTICS OF EUPHEMISMS IN ENGLISH AND AZERBAIJANI LANGUAGES
items.abstract: This article examines the linguacultural aspect in languages of different systems. Although the study of euphemisms began in the history of ancient Greek and Roman linguistics, a new era of their study began in the 20th century with the application of the anthropocentric method of research. The advent of cognitive linguistics also ushered in a new era of euphemism research. It was established that the pragmatic and linguacultural approach to euphemisms differed significantly from pre- 20th-century research in both content and the characteristics of communicative activity, as well as in its linguacultural nature. The essence was that, in addition to the general characteristics of euphemisms, their role in communicative activity began to be studied; the essence of semantic substitutions from the perspective of the speech act was revealed. It is noted that problems noted in English and Azerbaijani linguistics in the modern period have begun to be theoretically studied. It has been proven that, in particular, a linguacultural approach to euphemisms and the study of the fundamental concepts of cognitive linguistics in this context have given new impetus to the development of lexicology. This article has somewhat modernized the approach to the problem, provided a historical overview of euphemism research, and analyzed semantic associations and their cultural roots based on facts from the English and Azerbaijani languages. The complete formation of anthropocentric linguistics in linguistics at the end of the 20th century and the beginning of the 21st century created a turning point in the scientific study of euphemisms; the prominent feeling of the human factor in the study of the problem confirmed the necessity of pragmatic and linguocultural approaches to the problem. With the emergence of cognitive linguistics, no matter how many studies in these directions have increased and deep studies have been conducted, it is still impossible to consider the problem fully studied, as each research method emerges, it opens up new aspects of language problems, and as they are studied, cognitive linguistics is enriched with new theoretical facts.

items.title: Live‐Line Work on High‐Voltage Transmission Overhead Lines: From FRP Flashover to Air‐Gap Breakdown Physics and Emerging Technologies
items.abstract: ABSTRACT This paper presents a comprehensive review of live‐line work on high‐voltage transmission overhead lines, with a focus on insulation performance, air‐gap breakdown and discharge physics under realistic operating conditions. This review primarily covers journal publications from approximately 2014 to 2026, with emphasis on recent developments in the field. Despite the critical importance of live‐line maintenance for power system reliability, the number of peer‐reviewed journal studies remains relatively limited, and this work aims to consolidate the majority of available contributions within this period. Key topics include flashover mechanisms of fibreglass‐reinforced polymer hot sticks under cold and freezing conditions, physics‐based modelling of long air‐gap breakdown under switching‐impulse voltages and the influence of tower geometry, worker configuration and hybrid AC/DC systems on insulation performance. In addition, multi‐worker interaction, floating‐conductor effects, potential transfer mechanisms and high‐altitude conditions are examined. Fundamental discharge processes, including streamer inception, streamer‐to‐leader transition and leader propagation, are reviewed to establish a unified physical framework. Collectively, the reviewed studies demonstrate that live‐line insulation performance is governed by coupled electrostatic, thermal, environmental and geometric effects. This review provides a consolidated reference for the field, identifies the need for integrated multiphysics modelling approaches to improve safety criteria, standards development and minimum approach distance determination, and discusses emerging developments in helicopter‐assisted maintenance, advanced access techniques, monitoring and diagnostic technologies, artificial intelligence‐assisted tools and digital approaches that may contribute to safer and more efficient live‐line maintenance in future power systems.

items.title: LLM fine-tuning for international news style generation and cross-cultural dissemination quality assessment
items.abstract: The rapid globalization of news media has heightened the demand for high-quality, culturally adapted international news content. However, generating news articles that faithfully conform to the stylistic conventions of diverse national media outlets while maintaining cross-cultural semantic fidelity remains a formidable challenge. This paper presents a novel framework that leverages fine-tuned large language models (LLMs) for international news style generation and introduces a comprehensive cross-cultural dissemination quality assessment (CDQA) methodology. Specifically, we construct a multilingual international news corpus spanning seven major languages and ten distinct journalistic style profiles, drawn from leading international media organizations. We then apply parameter-efficient fine-tuning via Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) on a LLaMA-2-based backbone, augmented with a style-aware prefix adapter that conditions generation on target-style embeddings. For quality assessment, we propose a multi-dimensional evaluation framework integrating automatic metrics—including BLEU-4, ROUGE-L, and BERTScore—with a novel Cross-Cultural Appropriateness Score (CCAS) grounded in culturological theory. Experimental results demonstrate that our fine-tuned model achieves a BLEU-4 score of 42.7 and a BERTScore F1 of 0.876 on held-out test sets, outperforming strong baselines by 5.3 and 3.1 percentage points, respectively. Human evaluation conducted by bilingual journalists across five language pairs yields mean fluency and cultural appropriateness ratings of 4.21/5.00 and 4.08/5.00, respectively. Cross-cultural quality classification accuracy reaches 87.3%, validating the effectiveness of the CCAS framework. This work offers a scalable, reproducible pipeline for high-fidelity international news generation, with direct implications for global media localization.

items.title: LLM-Based Waypoint Authoring via Augmented Reality for Human–Robot Interaction
items.abstract: Augmented reality (AR) can make robot programming more intuitive by letting users set motion parameters directly in the workspace. This paper extends AURaPath, an AR system for interactive 6-DoF waypoint determination on a UR10 collaborative robot using HoloLens2, with a voice modality for hands-free authoring. The voice layer follows a two-tier design: an on-device keyword recognizer handles the safety-critical verbs behind a two-step confirmation gate, and a large language model (LLM) maps the resulting transcript to the system’s structured command set so that operators need not memorize fixed phrases; the deployed pipeline takes spoken microphone input, while the benchmark below evaluates the transcript-to-command mapping stage in isolation. We evaluate the mapping layer on an objective benchmark of 169 labeled utterances that isolates language-to-command mapping from speech recognition and robot execution, and we compare a deterministic keyword baseline, four local models on a single consumer GPU, and free-tier cloud backends. The keyword baseline cannot express parameterized authoring commands and scores zero on every authoring field, while a free-tier cloud model reaches 95.3% exact-match results, averaged over 10 runs. The reject analysis shows that the ability to decline out-of-scope input, rather than raw accuracy, determines whether a model is suitable for the language-mapping tier of our safety-gated architecture, in which a deterministic layer and a preview-before-execute gate remain responsible for execution, which supports keeping the safety-critical verbs on the deterministic layer. The benchmark selects the backend that the deployed system uses, on the same physical UR10 demonstrated in the base system. The project code, the evaluation harness and dataset, and the base-system demonstration are available on GitHub (Please see Data Availability Statement section).
