items.title: LLMDPA: pre-execution privacy auditing of DP-SGD via evidence-constrained semantic analysis
items.abstract: Abstract Privacy auditing has emerged as a critical component for safeguarding data privacy in machine learning models. Existing empirical auditing methods heavily rely on model runtime states or post-deployment interfaces, resulting in substantial time costs and limited source-level localization of leakage causes. In contrast, the theoretical guarantees of provable privacy mechanisms provide a basis for efficient privacy auditing with source-level traceability before model training. However, the validity of such auditing depends on the semantic consistency of the underlying implementation, which remains difficult for current automated methods to verify due to limited privacy-specific reasoning and explicit evidence modeling. To address this gap, we formalize the Pre-execution Privacy Auditing paradigm and instantiate it for DP-SGD through LLMDPA, an automated framework based on evidence-constrained semantic analysis. LLMDPA constructs a structured Evidence Chain to constrain LLM-based adjudication and identify hidden semantic failures in DP-SGD implementations. Evaluations on real-world and controlled benchmarks show that LLMDPA achieves global precision ranging from 98.82 to 100% and global F1-scores ranging from 0.9091 to 0.9677 across four LLM configurations, outperforming conventional static and vanilla LLM baselines. Moreover, LLMDPA audits a repository in approximately 50 s, providing a scalable and efficient complement to scale-sensitive attack evaluations. Overall, LLMDPA provides an interpretable and evidence-traceable instantiation of Pre-execution Privacy Auditing for DP-SGD.

items.title: Lost in the comments: Social context as a single‐pass jailbreak and defense on agentic platforms
items.abstract: Abstract As LLM‐based agents move onto multiagent platforms, they process direct prompts and surrounding social context—posts, comments, and upvotes—an attack surface that single‐turn alignment never addressed. We built a simulation of Moltbook, a social network for AI agents, and a pipeline turning 100 JailBreakBench goals into platform‐native posts with bystander comments of three valences: aggressive, ethical, and measured. Platform‐context reformatting alone raises the attack success rate (ASR) of GPT‐4o‐mini from 7% to 71%, beating a twenty‐query optimization baseline in one pass. Valence then acts as a bidirectional safety modulator: Ethical comments sharply suppress ASR, aggressive endorsements paradoxically reduce it by exposing intent, and measured, intellectually toned comments prove most dangerous, sustaining or elevating ASR. An ablation identifies valence rather than volume as key—a 35‐fold rise in upvotes leaves ASR unchanged—and every finding reproduces under an independent safety classifier with human adjudication. Ambiguous social context thus poses a greater threat than explicit pressure, while safety‐valenced signals offer a deployable defense for agentic platforms.

items.title: MACHINE AI AI-BASED MALFUNCTIONING INDUSTRIAL MACHINERY FAULT DETECTION AND MAINTENANCE REPORT SYSTEM
items.abstract: Abstract Industrial machines are used continuously in many manufacturing environments, so a small fault can quickly affect production, increase maintenance cost, or cause unexpected downtime. Bearing failure is a common example. Before a bearing becomes seriously damaged, the machine may start producing an unusual sound. Finding these changes by manual listening requires experience and regular monitoring. Machine AI was developed to support this task by analyzing machine sounds with artificial intelligence. The system accepts recorded machine audio or a WAV file and uses a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to decide whether the sound represents normal operation or a bearing fault. Industrial audio data, including the MIMII dataset, is used during model development. Librosa and SoundFile are used to prepare the audio, while PyTorch supports the machine-learning model. After the CNN gives a prediction, the result is sent through the Gemini API to a generative-AI module. Gemini prepares a maintenance report with the detected condition, possible causes, severity, and suggested actions. This gives the user more useful information than a fault label alone. The complete application is delivered through HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Flask, with a database for user details, audio-analysis results, predictions, and reports. Overall, Machine AI combines audio analysis, deep learning, and generative AI to support predictive maintenance in a practical web-based system. items.title: Machine learning analysis for the thermophoretic particle deposition in casson nanofluid with porous medium and heat generation
items.abstract: The aim of this work is to evaluate the impacts of heat generation on the radiative flow of Casson nanofluid over a sheet under LTNE circumstances while microbes are present, utilizing machine learning techniques based on the Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm. A simple method for moving tiny particles across a temperature gradient is thermophoretic particle deposition, which is essential for electrical and aerosol solution engineering. The energy equations are derived from the local thermal non-equilibrium to determine the unique thermal profiles of the solid and liquid phases. The current model, which combines the Levenberg-Marquardt method with AI-NN (artificial intelligence neural networks), offers a more complex computational solution than standard numerical methods. items.title: Machine Learning in Amyloidogenic Polypeptide Research: From Sequence Prediction to Drug Discovery
items.abstract: Abstract Over the past decade, machine learning (ML) has established a transformative paradigm for investigating amyloidogenic polypeptides. Characterized by their propensity to form ordered, β-sheet-rich fibrillar aggregates, these polypeptides are centrally implicated in the pathogenesis of numerous neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and Parkinson’s disease (PD). This review systematically evaluates the application of ML across critical domains of amyloid investigation: sequence-based amyloidogenicity prediction, structural biology, inhibitor design, and amyloid-related clinical objectives. We further summarize the diverse array of ML architectures currently employed in amyloid research, spanning classical algorithms (e.g., support vector machines and random forests) to advanced deep learning frameworks, such as the transformer framework, protein language models (PLMs), etc. Additionally, we spotlight emerging frontiers, namely, the integration of ML with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, the use of generative AI for de novo inhibitor design, etc., while addressing persistent bottlenecks in the field, including data standardization, model interpretability, and rigorous experimental validation for in silico predictions. Ultimately, this review serves as a foundational roadmap for emerging researchers and a definitive reference for established investigators operating at the intersection of artificial intelligence and amyloid biology.

items.title: MACHINE TRANSLATION POST-EDITING COMPETENCE IN THE AGE OF GENERATIVE AI: A CORPUS-BASED INVESTIGATION OF STUDENT TRANSLATORS' SKILLS
items.abstract: The main aim of the article is to investigate how translation students interact with AI-generated translations and examines the relationship between AI literacy and post-editing performance. Using a corpus-based mixed-methods approach, the study compares human translation, neural machine translation post-editing, and generative AI post-editing. The findings reveal that generative AI improves fluency and lexical diversity but introduces AI-specific challenges, including hallucinations and contextual distortions. Statistical analysis demonstrates that AI literacy, critical evaluation skills, and prompt formulation abilities significantly influence post-editing quality. The study proposes an AI-enhanced MTPE competence framework integrating linguistic, technological, evaluative, and collaborative dimensions. The results contribute to current discussions on translator competence and provide practical recommendations for translator education in AI-mediated environments. The study employs a mixed-methods research design combining corpus linguistics, quantitative statistical analysis, and qualitative thematic analysis. Data were collected from 60 undergraduate and graduate translation students divided into three groups: Human Translation (HT), Neural Machine Translation Post-Editing (NMTPE), and Generative AI Post-Editing (GAI-PE). The learner corpus consisted of approximately 90,000 words. Translation quality, error frequency, lexical diversity, and AI literacy indicators were analyzed using corpus tools and statistical procedures. The study expands traditional translation competence models by incorporating AI literacy, prompt engineering, hallucination detection, and human–AI collaboration as essential dimensions of MTPE competence. Unlike previous studies focusing mainly on translation quality and productivity, this research examines how AI-related competencies influence student translators' performance in generative AI environments. The findings indicate that generative AI enhances translation fluency and lexical richness while simultaneously creating risks associated with factual inaccuracies and hallucinations. AI literacy emerged as a significant predictor of post-editing performance, highlighting the growing importance of critical evaluation skills in translator training. The study concludes that future translator education should integrate AI literacy, prompt engineering, and critical assessment strategies to prepare students for technology-rich professional environments.

items.title: Making Healthcare AI Explainable: A Structured Review of Methods and Clinical Practice
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is rapidly transforming modern medicine, providing powerful tools to assist clinicians. However, the most accurate models are opaque, and their limited interpretability hinders clinical adoption and raises regulatory concerns. Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) aims to make these models’ decisions comprehensible. Despite its rapid growth and the many reviews already published, aspects such as the rigor of explanation evaluation, clinician involvement, and the use of large language models to generate explanations appear to have received limited attention. This article is a structured, relevance-prioritized review of XAI applied in healthcare, organized around six research questions covering the XAI techniques used, the data and clinical domains they are paired with, the models they explain, how evaluation is performed, the identified limitations, and the use of large language models. Unlike prior reviews that each address only part of this scope, we bring these dimensions together and quantify how rigorously explanations are evaluated and how often the underlying models are externally validated. We conducted a structured search across four literature sources: IEEE Xplore, PubMed, Google Scholar, and PubMed Central (PMC). We adapted the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) flow by carrying a relevance-prioritized subset forward to full-text eligibility assessment, yielding 64 articles for synthesis. Within this corpus, our review revealed a predominantly image-based, post hoc XAI landscape dominated by a few established methods such as SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM), and Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME), mostly paired with convolutional, tree-based, and hybrid models on classification and risk-prediction tasks. Clinicians evaluated the explanations in only a minority of the included studies, and relatively few models were externally validated, with no evidence of large language models in our corpus. We conclude that stronger evaluation practices and closer collaboration with clinicians are needed to produce models that are clinically useful and safe to deploy.

items.abstract: This article presents integrative indicators of two types for assessing the effectiveness of management of counteraction to destructive information network influence (DINI). The social factors of the multidimensionality of managerial activity at the meso, macro, and micro levels of society are described, which form the most complete picture of the current situation. The first type of indicators reflects the possibilities for objective assessment of the effectiveness of management of counteraction to DINI at the macro and meso levels of society in the most significant social spheres. The second type of indicators is oriented toward taking into account the significance of the human factor. The validity of the choice is evident in the implementation of the original sociological research program.

items.title: Managing the transformation of the cognitive potential of the economy through the introduction of generative AI as a personnel innovation in the face of labor shortages
items.abstract: The problem of structural labor shortages in the digital economy requires the implementation of breakthrough personnel innovations. Generative AI (GAI), which has automation and cognitive augmentation functions, is considered a strategic tool for managing the transformation of cognitive potential and compensating for labor shortages. The lack of quantitative assessment of the scale of labor shortage compensation through the dual effect (replacement and augmentation) of GAI in key sectors of the economy and the need to verify the strategic role of GAI as a personnel innovation are driving research on this issue. An assessment was conducted of the management of the transformation of the economy’s cognitive potential through the introduction of AI as a personnel innovation in conditions of a labour shortage. A comprehensive approach was applied, combining general scientific methods, statistical analysis, and economic mathematical modelling. The overall compensation of cognitive load through the implementation of generative AI in trade, manufacturing, and professional activities will amount to 5.752 million people in terms of headcount equivalent by 2027, which is more than four times the projected need to compensate for the structural deficit (1.4 million people). Generative AI acts not only as a means of covering the staffing deficit but also as a tool for the qualitative transformation of the economy’s cognitive potential, shifting the focus of employment to hybrid jobs and tasks that require a “human core” of competencies. For the first time, the concept of the “cognitive substitutability coefficient of GAI” (λGAI) has been proposed within the framework of the model of cognitive transformation of labor resources to quantitatively assess the total compensatory effect (automation + augmentation) of implementing GAI in the economy.

items.title: MANAJEMEN BUDAYA SEKOLAH DALAM PENGUATAN TATA KELOLA PENDIDIKAN PADA RPOGRAM KEAHLIAN TEKNIK MEKANIK INDUSTRI DI SMK CIBITUNG 1
items.abstract: The demand for quality graduates from Vocational High Schools (SMK) faces substantial challenges, notably institutional governance gaps and the weak integration of industrial values. This disparity reveals that vocational education governance has not been fully anchored in functionally integrated work culture cultivation. Consequently, this study aims to analyze school culture management in strengthening educational governance in the Industrial Mechanical Engineering (TMI) Expertise Program at SMK Cibitung 1 through planning, organizing, actuating, and controlling phases. A qualitative approach with a case study design was employed, gathering data through in-depth interviews, participatory observation, and documentation analysis. Data were analyzed interactively utilizing data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing/verification. The findings demonstrate that school culture management is systematically executed through POAC functions by integrating religious values, discipline, occupational health and safety (OHS), and the 5S/5R culture. This management model reinforces vocational governance by improving stakeholder participation, coordination transparency, and institutional accountability. The study concludes that the structured internalization of industrial culture serves as a strategic managerial foundation for achieving high-quality vocational education governance. Practical implications highlight the indispensability of formal industrial partnerships and exemplary leadership in institutionalizing a sustainable quality culture within vocational schools. ABSTRAK Tuntutan kualitas lulusan Sekolah Menengah Kejuruan (SMK) menghadapi tantangan serius berupa kesenjangan tata kelola kelembagaan dan rendahnya integrasi nilai-nilai kerja industri. Kesenjangan ini memperlihatkan bahwa tata kelola pendidikan vokasi belum sepenuhnya berlandaskan pada pembudayaan etos kerja yang terintegrasi secara fungsional. Oleh karena itu, penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis manajemen budaya sekolah dalam penguatan tata kelola pendidikan pada Program Keahlian Teknik Mekanik Industri (TMI) di SMK Cibitung 1 melalui tahapan perencanaan, pengorganisasian, pelaksanaan, dan evaluasi. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan desain studi kasus melalui wawancara mendalam, observasi partisipatif, serta analisis dokumentasi. Analisis data dilakukan secara interaktif dengan model kondensasi data, penyajian data, dan verifikasi simpulan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa manajemen budaya sekolah dilaksanakan secara sistematis melalui fungsi planning, organizing, actuating, dan controlling yang mengintegrasikan nilai religius, kedisiplinan, keselamatan dan kesehatan kerja (K3), serta budaya 5R (Ringkas, Rapi, Resik, Rawat, Rajin). Manajemen budaya sekolah terbukti memperkuat tata kelola pendidikan kejuruan melalui peningkatan partisipasi pemangku kepentingan, transparansi koordinasi, dan akuntabilitas kerja. Simpulan penelitian ini menegaskan bahwa internalisasi budaya industri yang terstruktur merupakan modal manajerial strategis dalam mewujudkan tata kelola kejuruan yang bermutu. Implikasi praktisnya menunjukkan pentingnya kemitraan industri formal dan keteladanan pimpinan dalam melembagakan budaya mutu di lingkungan sekolah kejuruan.

items.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to systematically map the vast body of academic literature on student-managed investment funds (SMIFs). It categorizes and indexes the research into a database, allowing scholars and practitioners to efficiently navigate decades of literature based on specific structural and operational characteristics. Design/methodology/approach This study employs an indexing methodology to organize the SMIF literature published between 1975 and 2025, classifying collected papers into three groups: surveys, case studies and general research. Findings The vast majority of SMIF research, 97 out of 126 papers included, are case studies. The index documents SMIF exploration from traditional equity and fixed-income investments into alternative assets such as venture capital and crypto assets and covers recent developments in environmental, social and governance investing and artificial intelligence adoption. Twelve surveys provide SMIF landscape snapshots. Nineteen general research papers discuss a wide range of topics such as challenges, fund performance and experiential learning. Institutions and faculty can use these findings to improve existing programs, while schools planning to start SMIFs can investigate various program structures and fund operation styles. Originality/value This study is the first to use an indexing approach to turn decades of SMIF literature into a structured database, acting as an archival “finding aid.” This preserves the operational details provided by fund insiders (the authors), empowering readers to quickly filter the literature and pinpoint the specific research papers that align with their interests.

items.title: Mapping the influence of artificial intelligence on the Ecuadorian judicial system from a human rights perspective. A scoping review
items.abstract: The objective was to map the existing scientific, regulatory, and doctrinal evidence on the influence of artificial intelligence on the Ecuadorian judicial system, with an emphasis on its relationship with the protection or possible violation of human rights. The methodology consisted of a scoping review, analyzing 16 articles that met the inclusion and exclusion criteria. The results show the artificial intelligence applications most frequently reported or proposed in the Ecuadorian justice system, the effect of artificial intelligence on human rights, and the risks of its adoption without specific regulations. It concludes that the immediate challenge for the Ecuadorian judicial system is to build a comprehensive legal framework for algorithmic governance, based on international human rights standards, in order to guarantee the transparency, explainability, and institutional accountability of artificial intelligence systems and thus minimize risks to the principles of due process, equality before the law, and effective judicial protection.

items.title: Matched-Context Group Policy Optimization for LLM Agent Training
items.abstract: Training long-horizon language model agents requires assigning credit to intermediate decisions from sparse terminal feedback. Within a finite group of sibling rollouts, useful action comparisons depend on their context, evidence for both alternatives, and how that evidence enters learning. We propose Matched-Context Group Policy Optimization (MCGPO), a procedure for constructing weighted action preferences from already collected trajectories. MCGPO defines comparison contexts with pre-action state summaries and observed rubric progress, annotated by task rules. Two-action support selects among ordered exact and coarse matching rules. Fixed folds separate candidate decisions from the terminal outcomes used to orient their preferences, and support-dependent evidence weights scale an auxiliary pairwise objective alongside shared GraphGPO task learning. MCGPO reuses rollout data and each response's original history, preserving critic-free training. Across six environment-backbone settings with three training seeds each, MCGPO improves mean success over matched GraphGPO: by 0.47-1.46 percentage points on ALFWorld and WebShop with Qwen2.5-1.5B and 7B, and by 3.96 and 5.16 points on WebShop with Qwen3-4B and 8B. The ALFWorld gains build on baseline success above 92%, where remaining headroom is limited. Integrated success improves in three of four Qwen2.5 settings. Three-seed factorial controls support opposite-fold evidence and evidence weighting; joint state-rubric matching achieves the highest mean in all four representation-control settings.

items.title: MathVis: Can AI Reason through Drawing? A Benchmark for Mathematical Figure Generation
items.abstract: This paper introduces MathVis, a benchmark designed to evaluate LLMs' ability to visualize frontier mathematical problems and perform diagram-assisted reasoning. The benchmark consists of 512 tasks, each comprising a mathematical statement, a reference diagram, executable TikZ or SVG code, a Gold Intermediate Representation (IR), atomic rubrics, and error codes. Through rigorous evaluation, GPT-6-Astra, Claude Fable 5, and Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview achieve pass@1 scores of 31.25%, 26.56%, and 22.85%, respectively. We found that although the tasks require visualization, LLMs produce outputs dominated by formal languages, symbols, and graphics programs, rather than explicit diagram-mediated reasoning. Furthermore, while the solutions generated by LLMs may contain all the necessary elements, they are often visually confusing to humans. Ultimately, this benchmark aims to visualize mathematical problems and promote research on enabling LLMs to simplify their reasoning via visual diagrams.

items.title: Measuring Visual Attention Across Concurrent and Sequential Visual Perception Tasks
items.abstract: Eye tracking provides a noninvasive method for measuring visual attention during human-computer interaction. Identifying which oculometric measures are most sensitive to different demands is important for the development of attention-aware systems. This pilot study examined whether common oculometric measures could distinguish between global, selective, and sustained visual attention tasks during low-demand viewing of static images. Ten participants (two males and eight females, 27.5 ± 4.7 years) completed descriptive, comparison-based, and memory-based visual tasks while wearing an eye tracker. Measures included task duration, fixation count, fixation percentage, blink count, blink percentage, and pupil diameter. Repeated-measures analyses showed a marginal effect of task condition on fixation count, with fixation counts descriptively highest during the global attention task and lowest during the selective attention task. Fixation percentage, blink measures, pupil diameter, and task duration did not significantly differ across conditions. These preliminary findings suggest that fixation count may be more sensitive to task-related attentional differences during low-demand visual interaction than blink- or pupil-based measures, supporting its potential use in future attention-aware and multimodal human-computer interaction systems.

items.title: Mechanistic Interpretability and Explainable AI (XAI) in Foundation Models: Reverse-Engineering Circuits, Superposition, and Safety Bounds
items.abstract: Abstract—Foundation models, particularly autoregressive Transformer Large Language Models (LLMs) and Vision-Language Models (VLMs), have exhibited unprecedented reasoning and generative capabilities across computer science and engineering. However, their internal representations operate as opaque, high-dimensional 'black boxes.' Conventional Explainable AI (XAI) techniques—predominantly post-hoc attribution methods such as Integrated Gradients, SHAP, and attention heatmap visualizations—fail to provide faithful causal explanations: they reflect output correlations rather than the internal mechanistic computations executing within the network, masking hazardous failure modes like latent hallucinations, sycophancy, and deceptive alignment. Mechanistic Interpretability has emerged as a rigorous bottom-up paradigm that seeks to reverse-engineer deep neural networks into human-understandable algorithmic circuits, decomposing polysemantic neuron activations into monosemantic features. This paper provides an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation of mechanistic interpretability and XAI for modern foundation models. We formalize the Linear Representation Hypothesis and the mathematics of neural superposition, analyze transformer residual streams as communicative communication buses, and model the discovery of specialized functional subgraphs—including induction heads, factual recall circuits, and indirect object identification (IOI) subnetworks. Furthermore, we evaluate Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) as an unsupervised mechanism to disentangle polysemantic latent spaces into overcomplete, monosemantic feature dictionaries. Finally, we implement an empirical evaluation testbed across open foundation models (Llama-3-8B, Gemma-2-9B, and Mistral-7B), quantitatively benchmarking causal scrubbing, activation patching, and SAE feature steering across mission-critical tasks (deceptive alignment detection, factual hallucination suppression, and jailbreak defense). Our findings demonstrate that activation patching isolates causal circuits responsible for 92.4% of factual routing, while SAE-guided feature clamping suppresses unfaithful hallucinations by 41.7% with less than 2.1% degradation in baseline perplexity. We conclude by formulating open challenges in circuit universality, superposition scaling laws, and regulatory verification under international AI governance frameworks. Index Terms—Mechanistic Interpretability, Explainable AI (XAI), Foundation Models, Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs), Polysemanticity, Neural Superposition, Induction Heads, Activation Patching, Transformer Circuits.

items.title: Mitigating Capability Degradation in LLM Self-Improvement via Representation Geometry Regularization
items.abstract: On-Policy Self-distillation is a self-improvement paradigm that enables large language models (LLMs) to improve their capabilities by leveraging the same model as both teacher and student under different conditioning contexts. However, we find that OPSD methods can progressively degrade previously acquired capabilities: queries that are correctly responded at earlier training stages may become incorrectly responded as optimization proceeds, even the overall performance continues to improve. Further analysis reveals that this degradation coincides with a deterioration of the geometry of hidden representations, characterized by reduced intra-cluster compactness and diminished inter-cluster separation. Motivated by this observation, we propose Representation Geometry Regularization (RGR), which preserves representation geometry during post-training by encouraging compactness within cluster and separation across cluster. RGR can be seamlessly integrated into existing OPSD methods without altering their core optimization procedures. Extensive experiments on multiple OPSD methods and benchmarks show that RGR generally alleviates capability degradation while retaining capability improvements. Our code is available in https://github.com/supermachinelearner/RGR.

items.title: Mobile Generative AI Literacy and English Writing Self-Efficacy: The Role of AI Feedback Engagement in Higher Education
items.abstract: This study examines the relationship between mobile Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) literacy and English writing self-efficacy (EWSE) among university students, with AI feedback engagement (AFE) proposed as a mediating mechanism. Using a quantitative cross-sectional design, data were collected from 312 university students in China through validated self-report measures. Partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) was employed to test the proposed relationships and mediation effects. The results show that mobile GenAI literacy (MGL) significantly predicts AFE (β = 0.563, p < 0.001) and EWSE (β = 0.182, p = 0.003), while AFE significantly predicts writing self-efficacy (β = 0.478, p < 0.001). AFE partially mediates the relationship between MGL and writing self-efficacy, accounting for approximately 59.6% of the total effect. The model explains 41.2% of the variance in writing self-efficacy. These findings indicate that the educational value of MGL extends beyond technological competence, with active engagement in AI-generated feedback serving as an important mechanism for strengthening writing confidence. The study highlights the importance of pedagogical approaches that promote critical evaluation, reflective use, and meaningful engagement with AI feedback.

items.title: MoPrO-SD: Modular Prompt Optimization for Stance Detection
items.abstract: Stance detection remains challenging for large language models (LLMs) due to implicit opinions, sarcasm, and context-dependent expressions of stance. Although automatic prompt optimization offers an alternative to fine-tuning without updating model parameters, existing structured approaches are not specifically designed around stance-label semantics and class-specific ambiguities. We introduce MoPrO-SD, a stance-specific prompt optimization framework that decomposes prompts into functional semantic modules and refines them sequentially using LLM-based feedback. We study three refinement strategies: instruction-only optimization (I), instruction with reasoning (I+R), and instruction with per-example reasoning (I+R+E), using class-conditioned errors for stance-label refinement. We also introduce VaccineStance, a new human-annotated benchmark for vaccine stance detection. Experiments across four datasets and five open-weight LLMs show that MoPrO-SD improves upon the human-written Base prompt in many settings. On SemEval-2016, class-conditioned feedback achieves higher mean Macro-F1 than pooled feedback for four of five backbones. Both reasoning-based strategies, I+R and I+R+E, achieve strong performance, with their relative effectiveness varying across models and datasets, while remaining competitive with recent prompt optimization methods. The MoPrO-SD code and VaccineStance dataset are available on GitHub.

items.title: Multi-Modal Graph Neural Network-Inspired Vessel Identification and Tracking for UAV-Based Maritime Surveillance
items.abstract: The unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based maritime surveillance is becoming an important part of maritime Internet of Things (IoT) and intelligent transportation systems. It provides a flexible and cost-effective way to large-scale maritime traffic monitoring. However, achieving robust situational awareness remains challenging in practical maritime environments. The main challenges arise from heterogeneous sensing modalities, adverse imaging conditions, and spatial misalignment caused by UAV motion. To address these problems, this paper proposes an airborne multi-modal graph learning-driven framework, termed AMGT, for vessel identification and tracking in UAV-assisted maritime IoT. Specifically, visible and infrared images are first aligned and fused through a multi-parameter perspective transformation model. This improves visual perception under low visibility and complex illumination conditions. Automatic identification system (AIS) messages are then temporally synchronized using interpolation and linear prediction. To detect small and oriented vessels, we develop a mixed-modality MAir-YOLOv8-OBB detector, followed by the MAir-SORT algorithm for stable vessel tracking. We further design a graph learning-driven association network to model temporal dynamics and spatial dependencies among vessels and between vessels and UAVs. A motion-aware coordinate unification (MCU) strategy is also introduced to reduce nonlinear misalignment caused by UAV motion. Experiments on the MAP-M2UAV50 dataset show that AMGT achieves high accuracy and efficiency. The results demonstrate its potential for UAV-assisted maritime IoT applications, including vessel monitoring, traffic situational awareness, and intelligent maritime transportation services. The dataset and code will be available at https://github.com/MAPGroup/AMGT.

items.title: Multidisciplinary collaboration and workflows on Heritage Building Information Modelling (HBIM) projects: a framework for improvement
items.abstract: Heritage Building Information Modelling (HBIM) projects face significant challenges, especially in relation to multidisciplinary collaboration and project workflows.This paper examines HBIM work processes, presenting a practical framework to improve HBIM workflows and multidisciplinary collaboration occurring on construction heritage projects. Design/methodology/approachAn initial deductive literature review provides a foundation for the study by identifying thematic HBIM industry challenges.An inductive, interpretivist and qualitative examination of HBIM combines survey questionnaire with case study and in-depth interviews to provide a holistic understanding of the opportunities and challenges confronting practitioners. FindingsFindings indicate that HBIM offers great potential for improving heritage protection, but challenges around data management; human factors; technical issues and training skills remain.A resulting framework for improvement identifies five key outcomes around which improvement depends: team coordination; sharing of knowledge; standards and industry specifications; technical tools and training/education.Recommendations are rooted to case study evidence and practitioner opinion; the paper highlighting the need for further research to refine practices globally. OriginalityThe research makes a contribution to the Heritage Building Information Modelling (HBIM) literature through the focused analysis of project work processes and multidisciplinary collaboration, resulting in an improvement framework for industry.The combination of literature review analysis, survey findings, case study examination and practitioner interviews provides a reliable dataset for the arguments made.

items.title: Multimodal Deep Learning for Participatory Public Art Assessment: Integrating Computer Vision and Behavioral Analytics for Community Engagement
items.abstract: In this work, a deep learning-based multimodal framework for evaluating public engagement with public art is introduced by combining computer vision and behavioral analysis. Existing multimodal models have primarily been applied in domains such as educational settings and behavior analysis, while their application to public art assessment remains limited by challenges in representing subjective human factors, complex behaviors, and interactions across modalities. To address these challenges, the proposed framework employs a Transformer-based architecture to integrate multimodal information and model cross-modal interactions. Image and video inputs representing artworks and participant behaviors, including movement, gaze, and interaction, are processed using 3D convolutional neural networks to extract spatiotemporal features, followed by modality-specific encoding and adaptive fusion using cross-attention. The framework generates outputs related to engagement, emotion recognition, and interaction assessment. For component-level evaluation before real-world public art deployment, the framework was evaluated on three complementary benchmark datasets: NTU RGB+D, Kinetics-700, and AVA (Aesthetic Visual Analysis), representing behavioral, activity recognition, and aesthetic perception tasks. In the classification task, the accuracy obtained was 92.0% and the F1-score of 0.909 for NTU RGB+D, while that of Kinetics-700 was 89.0% and the F1-score of 0.878. The AVA dataset was evaluated using aesthetic-score regression, yielding a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.87. These findings provide component-level evidence of computational effectiveness but do not constitute end-to-end validation in real-world public art settings.

items.title: Multivariate Stock Time-Series Forecasting Using an Improved Transformer
items.abstract: As financial markets become increasingly digital and intelligent, stock-price forecasting has emerged as an important topic in financial engineering, artificial intelligence, and data mining. Stock prices are shaped by firm fundamentals, macroeconomic conditions, investor sentiment, and market policies, while also exhibiting strong nonlinearity, nonstationarity, and noise. Extracting useful information from historical financial data and developing accurate and stable forecasting models therefore remain challenging. This study proposes an improved Transformer for multivariate stock time-series forecasting that combines feature-gated embedding with a residual prediction head. Daily data for Apple (AAPL), Microsoft (MSFT), and Google (GOOG) were obtained from the public YFinance interface for the period from January 1, 2000, to January 1, 2020. The model uses eight features—Open, High, Low, Close, Volume, RSI, ATR, and MACD—from the previous 30 trading days to predict the closing price five trading days ahead. A strictly chronological split, training-set-only normalization, and separate sliding-window construction are adopted to prevent look-ahead leakage. The proposed model is compared with Persistence, residual XGBoost, LSTM, a vanilla Transformer, and a standard feature-gated Transformer through the main experiment, cross-stock generalization tests, an ablation study, and a supplementary return-prediction experiment. On AAPL, the model achieves an RMSE of 1.2712, an MAE of 0.9242, and a MAPE of 2.5268%, slightly outperforming Persistence and residual XGBoost. It performs nearly identically to Persistence on GOOG and is slightly weaker than Persistence and residual XGBoost on MSFT, while consistently outperforming the LSTM and Transformer-based deep-learning baselines. These results demonstrate the accuracy and stability of the proposed model.

items.title: Nanomaterials in Agriculture and Their Potential Hazards: A Review
items.abstract: Nanomaterials are increasingly applied in modern agriculture to improve crop productivity, nutrient efficiency, and plant protection through fertilizers, pesticides, and delivery systems. However, their growing implementation raises significant concerns regarding environmental fate, ecological toxicity, and potential risks to human health. This review aims to (i) summarize current knowledge on nanomaterial applications in agriculture and (ii) critically evaluate their associated environmental and health risks. The manuscript integrates evidence on nanoparticle behavior in soil–plant–water systems, including transport, transformation, uptake, and accumulation across trophic levels. Particular attention is given to key toxicity mechanisms such as oxidative stress, membrane damage, genotoxicity, and bioaccumulation across terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems. The review also highlights limitations of current studies, which are predominantly short-term and laboratory-based, lacking long-term field validation and standardized risk assessment approaches. Emerging approaches such as artificial intelligence-based optimization and commercial nano-enabled agricultural products, along with existing regulatory frameworks, are further discussed. By integrating agronomic, toxicological, and regulatory perspectives, this review provides a comprehensive systems-level overview of nano-enabled agriculture, emphasizing the urgent need for harmonized risk assessment methodologies, long-term environmental monitoring, and interdisciplinary research.

items.title: Narcissistic traits and emotional dependence on large language models among adolescents
items.abstract: Background This study examined associations between narcissistic traits and emotional dependence on large language models (LLMs) among adolescents, focusing on anxiety and physical activity. Methods A multistage stratified sample of 1622 Chinese junior high school students was surveyed in November 2025. Narcissistic traits, anxiety, LLM emotional dependence, and physical activity were assessed using the FFNI-SF, GAD-2, an adapted five-item LLM emotional dependence measure, and PARS-3, respectively. Pearson correlations and PROCESS Models 4 and 7 with 5,000 bootstrap resamples were conducted, with Johnson–Neyman analysis used to probe the interaction. Results Narcissistic traits correlated positively with anxiety (r=0.118, P<0.001) and LLM emotional dependence (r=0.301, P<0.001), while anxiety correlated positively with LLM emotional dependence (r=0.146, P<0.001). Physical activity correlated negatively with anxiety (r=−0.119, P<0.001) and LLM emotional dependence (r=−0.075, P = 0.002). Adjusting for grade and left-behind status, anxiety showed a small indirect association between narcissistic traits and LLM emotional dependence (Effect=0.011, 95% CI [0.004, 0.020]). The narcissistic traits × physical activity interaction was significant (β=−0.056, P = 0.015), with the narcissism–anxiety association significant below 0.73 SD of physical activity. The moderated mediation index was not significant (Index=−0.0061, 95% bootstrap CI [−0.0130, 0.0001]). Conclusion Narcissistic traits were positively associated with adolescent LLM emotional dependence, with a small cross-sectional indirect association through anxiety. Physical activity moderated the narcissism–anxiety association, although overall moderated mediation was not supported.

items.title: Network Topology Shapes AI Intervention Effectiveness on Deception: Truth-Telling vs. Investigative Agents
items.abstract: Deploying AI agents to combat dishonest communication is an intuitive response to deception in hybrid human-AI societies. However, the efficacy of such interventions in realistic networked settings remains unclear. We study this problem using an evolutionary game-theoretic model of the Deceiver's Game by extending it to structured networks, where agents can adopt deception, truth-telling, and investigation strategies. We introduce committed AI agents (zealots) fixed to either truth-telling or investigative strategies and conduct agent-based simulations across three network topologies. Our key findings are: (1) passive committed truth-telling agents can amplify adaptive deception by creating exploitable honest partners, whereas investigative agents increase adaptive truth-telling in the oscillatory regime; (2) intervention effects are non-monotonic in deployment density because committed agents reshape rather than simply suppress the underlying oscillatory dynamics; and (3) response peaks depend on topology, with sampled scale-free populations showing sharp low-density responses and fully connected populations requiring larger committed fractions. Overall, the results highlight the need to distinguish passive truth-telling from active investigation when using committed agents to influence networked deception dynamics.

items.title: Neuromarketing in the Digital Age
items.abstract: Neuromarketing is a multidisciplinary field that aims to better understand consumer behaviour at the intersection of neuroscience and marketing. The current trend in academic literature indicates that strategies should focus not only on technological elements but also on human neurological responses. The evolution of marketing communication towards the integration of social media and artificial intelligence technologies requires learning the mechanisms underlying social media behaviour. Social media interactions affect the brain's reward system, while the excessive data density in digital media increases cognitive load, and artificial intelligence-supported algorithms reinforce cognitive biases. Neuromarketing tools integrated with artificial intelligence will facilitate the development of personalised and real-time marketing strategies by analysing subconscious processes more quickly and easily.

items.title: Next-Generation Water Quality Monitoring via Artificial Intelligence-Coupled Nanozymes
items.abstract: Abstract Safe water management requires rapid and highly sensitive analytical platforms capable of detecting contaminants in complex environmental matrices. Nanozymes are nanomaterials with enzyme-mimicking catalytic activity that offer remarkable advantages for field-deployable sensing, including stability and compatibility with portable formats. However, conventional nanozyme sensors often exhibit nonlinear catalytic behavior, limited selectivity, and susceptibility to interference in natural waters. This Perspective evaluates how integrating artificial intelligence (AI) with nanozyme-based systems can resolve these constraints. We analyze mechanistic nanozyme responses to major pollutant classes, including heavy metals, dyes, pharmaceuticals, and pesticides, and show how machine learning and deep learning models enhance sensitivity, mitigate matrix effects, and enable multiplex classification via catalytic fingerprints. We further highlight emerging AI-enabled architectures, including smartphone analytics, Internet of Things (IoT)-based nanozyme devices, and cloud-connected autonomous monitoring systems. Finally, we discuss the potential of standardized datasets, digital-twin simulations, and AI-driven design of single-atom nanozymes to advance global water quality assessment.

items.abstract: Large Language Model agents have made it possibleto talk with digital tools using everyday language but creatingsystems that are dependable and safe requires good organizationof models, integration of tools in parts and careful control ofhow the system runs. This paper introduces NEXUS, a personalproductivity agent that uses the Model Context Protocol (MCP)to carry out tasks that need steps through natural-languageconversation. NEXUS uses Google Gemini as its LLM anduses Groq-hosted Llama 3.3 70B as a backup model givinga second way to think when the main model fails. NEXUSfollows a Think–Act–Observe routine: first NEXUS reads theuser’s request then NEXUS decides what action is needed thenNEXUS asks the tool via MCP then NEXUS checks the outcomeand finally NEXUS writes the response. NEXUS works withFilesystem, To-Do and Web Search MCP services. The customTo-Do service stores task data in SQLite lets users manage taskskeeps a log of changes and allows undo actions. NEXUS also hasa Human-in-the-Loop feature that asks the user to confirm beforeany change that alters the system state is carried out. NEXUScan also start tasks on its own. Can communicate with outsidesystems through its built-in services. By keeping the thinking partof the LLM separate, from the tool actions and by using modelbackup and strict tool controls NEXUS offers a system that’smodular, dependable and able to grow for personal productivity.

items.title: Non-linear Burnout Trajectory and Academic Motivation Across Training Stages in Obstetrics and Gynecology Residency
items.abstract: Background: Burnout is prevalent among postgraduate medical trainees, yet stage-stratified data in obstetrics and gynecology (Ob-Gyn) residency remain sparse. The relationship between burnout domains and academic motivation has not been examined in this population. Objectives: To map burnout prevalence and domain severity across four stages of an Ob-Gyn residency program and examine associations between burnout domains and academic motivation subtypes. Methods: This cross-sectional study enrolled 94 Ob-Gyn residents (semesters 2–9) from the Faculty of Medicine, Universitas Airlangga, undergoing clinical training at a major tertiary teaching hospital in Surabaya, Indonesia. Instruments included the Maslach-Trisni Burnout Inventory and Academic Motivation Scale. Results: Overall burnout prevalence was 25.5%, varying markedly across stages: 44.0% (Stage I), 28.0% (Stage II), 7.4% (Stage III), and 23.5% (Stage IV) (p=0.026), forming a non-linear, U-shaped trajectory. Stage I exhibited significantly higher emotional exhaustion than Stage III (p=0.033). Personal accomplishment (PA) positively correlated with all intrinsic motivation subtypes and introjected/identified regulation and negatively with amotivation (p<0.05). External regulation declined from Stage I to IV (p=0.032), independently of burnout. Conclusions: Burnout concentrates at early and late training stages rather than accumulating uniformly. PA co-occurs with autonomous motivation, suggesting a protective resource-like role. Stage-specific interventions and reinforcement of residents’ clinical competence are warranted.

items.title: Not Just an Evaluation: A Case Study of Discourse Particle Sensitivity in Language Models
items.abstract: Discourse particles subtly shape the flow of discourse by reflecting conversational context and interlocutor attitudes, often leaving the truth-conditional meaning untouched. They are also often polyfunctional, with distinct senses which partially overlap with other particles; for example, the exclusive use of English "just" and "only" ("John only/just drinks water"). Despite the frequency of these words in natural language, they have gone largely unstudied due to the subtle nature of their effects. We investigate LLM sensitivity to "just" and "only" in natural conversations using behavioral and mechanistic analyses. First, we find that LLMs and humans similarly prefer the presence of these particles in context, and both are more sensitive to "just" compared to "only". Second, when sampling from LLMs with and without these particles, we find LLMs consistently rate generations as more likely, given their source context, demonstrating their particle sensitivity. In both experiments, instruction tuning increases sensitivity. Finally, we localize particle-sensitive units within LLMs and find the overlap between "just" and "only" is asymmetric: "only" units transfer selectively to exclusive "just", while all "just" units transfer to "only" equally well regardless of sense, suggesting LLM lexical-level particle representations are partially organized by sense. We release our code, sense-labeled dialogue stimuli, and human preference annotations at https://github.com/JiahuiKChen/Not_Just_an_Evaluation.

items.title: Novel Approaches to Language Assessment Part 1: Artificial Intelligence–Automated Scoring of a Sentence Recall Task for School-Age Children
items.abstract: PURPOSE: Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies have the potential to enhance the delivery of speech-language pathology services. One area of practice that could benefit from AI is automated screenings for developmental language disorder (DLD) in early elementary students. This report presents the elements and processes involved in evaluating an AI-based automated scoring system using archival recordings. METHOD: A total of 947 audio samples of children completing the Redmond Sentence Recall (RSR) task, representing cases with and without DLD, were used. We developed an automated version of the RSR (AutoRSR), employing automated speech recognition (ASR), natural language processing, and machine learning models, to automate the tasks of transcribing recordings, tracking the number of errors children produced, scoring production accuracies based on RSR criteria, and generating pass/fail decisions based on age-referenced expectations against a reference standard (i.e., Core Language scores from the Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals-Fourth Edition for a subset of 130 children). Different speech recognition models (Whisper and Reverb ASR) were applied to examine potential trade-offs. The accuracy of the AutoRSR was compared to human scoring. RESULTS: AutoRSR with Whisper speech recognition yielded sensitivity = .768 and specificity = .784, whereas Reverb speech recognition yielded sensitivity = .873 and specificity = .730. While AutoRSR had some mismatches with human evaluators and tended to produce lower scores, it converged more closely with the reference standard than human-scored protocols. CONCLUSIONS: AI technologies have become powerful enough to automate the scoring of recordings of children's sentence recall with similar accuracy levels as human evaluators. Next steps are discussed. SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL: https://doi.org/10.23641/asha.34050876.

items.title: Nursing Through Change: Experiences of Brazilian Female Nurses over 40 with a Digital Interaction Tool, a Secondary Qualitative Analysis
items.abstract: Background: Digital communication tools change how hospital staff request services and follow up patients’ needs. Their value depends on how well they fit everyday work. Women over 40 may bring experience of successive technological changes, but age alone says little about professional seniority or digital confidence. Objective: To understand how Brazilian nurses over 40 perceive the effects of a digital interaction tool on their nursing work. Design: Secondary qualitative analysis informed by Braun and Clarke’s reflexive thematic analysis. Setting: A large hospital in São Paulo, Brazil. Participants: Ten Brazilian female nurses aged 41–55, selected from 20 interviews on the basis of age and explicitly recorded female identification. One additional interview requires eligibility confirmation. Methods: A second review of a pool of participants followed Braun & Clarke’s six thematic analysis phases: familiarization with data, generating initial codes, searching for themes, reviewing themes, defining and naming themes, and writing the report. Results: Four themes were developed: learning again without starting from scratch; no longer the go-between for every request; when a digital request still needs a phone call; and making work visible without losing personal contact. Participants described easier communication and greater team autonomy, alongside the effort of learning another system, duplicated requests and dependence on other departments’ responses. Comparisons with telephone communication and replacement platforms showed how they assessed successive changes in their working practices. Conclusions: Participants valued the tool when it reduced the need to relay requests and helped them organize care. Its usefulness diminished when they still had to telephone, repeat information or chase a response. Continuing support, integration between systems and clear departmental responsibilities warrant attention. These accounts do not establish an objective reduction in workload or effects specific to age or gender. The analysis remains subject to the research team’s reflexive review.

items.title: NutriEpiDB: a database for dietary compounds with epigenetic targets
items.abstract: Understanding the relationship between dietary compounds and epigenetic mechanisms is central to research in nutrigenomics and human health. Structured datasets that systematically integrate dietary, molecular, and epigenetic information are essential for reproducible and data-driven investigation in this domain. This dataset compiles curated associations between 653 unique dietary compounds, 585 food sources, and 80 epigenetic targets, extracted from 1,963 primary research articles identified through systematic searches in PubMed and Web of Science. Compound identification was performed via large language model-assisted extraction and subsequently standardized using PubChem, RDKit, and semantic clustering procedures. Binding affinity data were incorporated for human proteins with validated epigenetic function, prioritizing records with quantitative measures. Variables are harmonized and annotated using recognized chemical and biological ontologies. This resource supports research on nutriepigenomics, compound–mechanism associations, and food-derived bioactives, enabling hypothesis generation, validation studies, and data mining in nutritional, biomedical, and computational research contexts.

items.title: Occupational Wearable Robotics
items.abstract: Injuries and occupational diseases represent an important economic factor in different industrial sectors. In Italy alone, there have been over 60000 confirmed cases of occupational diseases in 2022, where musculoskeletal disorders (MSD) represent 70% of the total. This fact highlights the importance of protecting workers against physical efforts. While current ergonomic tools can mitigate most of the risk factors, there is still a non-negligible number of tasks that cannot be completely compensated for. This is due to the high complexity and costs of the workplace reorganization, or simply strict requirements of the target task. In some of these cases, exoskeletons are a viable solution. This chapter introduces different kinds of existing exoskeletons, with particular focus on occupational exoskeletons, considering commercial systems already deployed in industry, and some of the most promising technologies which will arrive in the next years. The deployment of occupational exoskeletons is conditioned by the regulatory frameworks and by the required reorganization of the workplace. Both concepts and the latest developments are discussed in this chapter, including their integration into Industry 4.0. Finally, this chapter describes the most common evaluation methods and discusses current efforts toward standardized benchmarking methods which will allow evaluating the benefit of using exoskeletons in real applications.

items.title: Olfactory dysfunction among gas station employees exposed to fuel vapors using digital odor identification testing
items.abstract: Gas station employees are chronically exposed to fuel vapors containing benzene, toluene, ethylbenzene, and xylene (BTEX), and other volatile organic compounds (VOCs), raising occupational concerns about olfactory function. In this cross-sectional study, 116 Brazilian gas station employees (86 men and 30 women; median age, 37.5 years; range, 19–58) completed a questionnaire and underwent objective olfactory assessment with the MultiScent-20 digital odor identification test. Overall, 58.6% had olfactory dysfunction, including 46.6% with hyposmia and 12.1% with anosmia, whereas only 23.3% reported that their work affected their sense of smell. Longer employment duration was associated with lower olfactory scores (Spearman's ρ = −0.41; p < 0.001) and independently increased the odds of dysfunction (odds ratio [OR] = 1.15 per additional year; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.06–1.26; p = 0.003). These findings support incorporating olfactory assessment into occupational health surveillance for workers chronically exposed to fuel vapors.

items.title: OMNI_BUILD INTELLIGENCE An LLM-Based Framework for Constraint-Aware Architectural Floor-Plan Generation, Visualization, and Interactive Project Management
items.abstract: The increasing capability of large language models (LLMs) creates an opportunity to redesign how users interact with computational design software. Architectural planning is a particularly relevant domain because early-stage requirements are often expressed in natural language, while the resulting design must ultimately be represented as geometry. This paper presents Omni Build Intelligence, an implemented full-stack prototype that explores an LLM-assisted workflow for generating preliminary architectural floor plans from structured user requirements. The system accepts building type, requested room count, plot width and length, and special requirements. A Flask backend constructs a domain-specific prompt and invokes a Llama 3.3 70B model through the Grok API. The response is expected in a structured textual format containing rooms, coordinates, dimensions, door relationships, and a summary. The generated representation is parsed into easy for software to read objects and passed to a React interface. The interface provides a two-dimensional blueprint view and an isometric three-dimensional visualization. A conversion layer transforms generated room rectangles into editable wall and label primitives that can be associated with a project record. The broader platform also includes authentication, project management, plot listing and filtering, dashboard functionality, and persistence of drawing data. These components make Omni Build more than a standalone text-generation demonstration: it is a prototype for integrating generative AI into an interactive design workflow. The research contribution of this paper is the formulation of a rigorous evaluation methodology for such a system. The proposed methodology defines an Architectural Requirement Prompt Dataset, meaningful baselines, formal geometric constraints, automated validation metrics, human evaluation criteria, ablation experiments, and statistical analysis procedures. Metrics include constraint satisfaction, boundary violations, room overlap, requirement accuracy, dimension validity, space use of space, valid-plan rate, and generation latency. A user guided study is proposed to evaluate perceived practicality and usefulness. The study deliberately does not claim measured superiority because the repository provides implementation evidence but not a completed controlled benchmark. Instead, the paper establishes a reproducible experimental framework through which the system can be evaluated. This distinction prevents software functionality from being mistaken for research evidence. The work concludes that LLM-based architectural assistance is most appropriately positioned as an early-stage design aid whose natural-language flexibility is combined with explicit geometric validation and human review. Keywords: large language models, generative AI, computer based architectural design, floor-plan generation, constraint based prompting, spatial reasoning, structured generation, user guided design, interactive visualization, project management

items.title: One AI Approval Is Not Unlimited Authority: Reality-Gated Execution for Frontier AI and Critical Systems
items.abstract: An AI agent receives permission to execute a command. But what if the command reaches the wrong destination, the payment follows a compromised route, or a robotic actuator behaves differently from what was authorized? Should that original permission still allow the system to continue? As frontier AI models and autonomous agents increasingly control financial transactions, cloud infrastructure, sensitive communications, software deployments, industrial equipment, robotics, and critical systems, conventional authorization faces a fundamental limitation: permission to execute does not establish that the intended real-world effect actually occurred. This paper examines a different approach to machine authority: “A permit to effect once is not a permit to effect permanently.” Building on the principle that “Computation is not authority to act,” the proposed architecture introduces a further requirement: authority to continue must be earned through independently verified evidence of a preceding real effect. The paper presents a safety-first execution-finality architecture based on Receipt-Gated Interim Effectuation Validation (IEV). Instead of immediately releasing the full consequence of a high-risk operation, the system can authorize a deliberately bounded real effect on the actual operational path. A protected observer, destination, transaction system, network component, or hardware controller produces evidence of what actually occurred. An independent Interim Effectuation Validator examines that evidence against the authorized act, expected outcome, destination, scope, freshness, policy, and revocation state. Only successful validation establishes the protected continuation condition required for the next phase. In stronger realizations, this is not merely another software approval. The cryptographic material required to complete the next effect is unavailable until the preceding real-world effect has been independently verified. Continuation may depend on receipt-bound key derivation, split credentials, protected state transitions, threshold approvals, hardware registers, or other protected enforcement mechanisms. The validator does not relay the original command, and an agent's own assertion of success is never a substitute for required independent evidence. The paper consolidates 35 execution-finality workflow profiles (E01–E35) spanning eight broad technical families, including: AI agents, autonomous tool execution, frontier model deployment, and credential control. Financial transactions, payment verification, settlement, and protected value release. Messages, file transfers, confidential data disclosure, and destination verification. Cloud infrastructure, database mutations, software updates, and persistent AI memory. Robotics, industrial automation, autonomous vehicles, and unmanned aerial systems. Telecommunications, radio transmission, satellite operations, and network control. GPUs, accelerators, hardware enforcement, and protected execution domains. Distributed effectuation, quorum validation, uncertain outcomes, and recovery. The architecture also examines 12 implementation-equivalence and design-around closures, addressing attempts to bypass the protected causal dependency through alternate execution paths, substituted components, software–hardware rearrangements, or different credential and validation topologies. A dedicated Safety-First Critical-System Profile establishes that execution correctness, consequence containment, and mandatory validation take precedence over minimizing latency. Optimizations remain possible, but they must preserve the protections selected for the relevant consequence class. A further distinction is made between simulation and actual effectuation. A successful simulation cannot establish that the real recipient, network route, transaction destination, or physical actuator will behave as expected. The proposed staged mechanism therefore uses bounded effects on the actual consequence-capable path, subject to protected observation and explicit safety assumptions. When evidence is missing, conflicting, stale, replayed, or indeterminate, ordinary continuation remains unavailable. Unknown outcomes require reconciliation, bounded remediation, safe-state handling, or protected escalation—not automatic success or blind retry. The central research question is straightforward: Should a high-consequence autonomous machine be permitted to cause its next irreversible effect before independently verifying what happened during its previous authorized effect? This publication proposes that, for selected high-risk operations, real-world evidence should become a technical and cryptographic prerequisite for continuing execution—not merely an audit record produced after the consequences have occurred. The paper is a technical architecture and analytical contribution. It does not report experimental deployment, measured security improvements, or empirical validation. Its proposed properties depend on assumptions concerning evidence integrity, protected authority, enforcement-path completeness, and atomic consumption of continuation authority. Patent pending: Indian Patent Office application 202631117633, “Systems and Methods for Cryptographically Staged Effectuation with Verified Partial Effect, Receipt-Bound Full Effectuation, and Software-Hardware Enforcement.” This publication makes no assertion that any particular commercial system implements the architecture and does not establish patentability, infringement, ownership, or priority. Invitation for Independent Technical Review Researchers, frontier AI model providers, cloud and hardware engineers, security architects, patent professionals, and critical-infrastructure specialists are invited to examine the 35 workflows, test the security assumptions, identify relevant prior art, challenge the anti-bypass properties, and evaluate whether receipt-dependent execution authority provides meaningful additional protection for consequential autonomous systems. Critical feedback, adversarial analysis, alternative engineering approaches, and independent conclusions are welcome.

items.title: One Thing Leads to Another: The Essentials of Time Series Causal Discovery
items.abstract: Time series causal discovery --- the process of detecting causation between time series --- has its roots in signal processing research from over a half century ago. It has since received active and widespread interest, evolving into different forms across domains such as statistics, dynamical systems and machine learning. Entering this fragmented and constantly evolving research landscape can be daunting. This tutorial provides a unified overview of time series causal discovery across research communities. We introduce the key principles invoked by modern discovery methods, and we discuss their limitations and assumptions. We also discuss how discovery methods are evaluated, benchmarked and fine-tuned. We further discuss how causal discovery for time series is becoming crucial for downstream tasks in agriculture and Earth science, in healthcare, and in artificial intelligence systems. We believe that this tutorial will serve as a valuable resource in navigating the deluge of recent causality research, as well as an invitation to signal processing audiences to contribute to causal problems. To further help readers, we host a companion repository to link to useful code packages and resources at https://github.com/CHAI-UK/Awesome-Time-Series-Causal-Discovery.

items.title: Online dispute resolution for crypto-asset disputes: AI, smart 1 contracts and digital inclusion by design
items.abstract: Crypto-asset disputes create distinctive barriers to effective remedies because they combine technical opacity, cross-border legal fragmentation, pseudonymous actors, irreversible transactions and uncertain enforcement pathways. These barriers are especially significant for vulnerable and non-expert users, who may be unable to identify the legally relevant harm, organize blockchain-based evidence, select an appropriate forum or obtain practical enforcement. This article develops a conceptual, normative and legal-design proposal for a hybrid Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) architecture that integrates off-chain artificial intelligence (AI) assistance with a minimized on-chain smart-contract layer. The model assigns AI systems a supporting role in legal information, triage, claim classification, evidence organization, explanation and negotiation, while reserving contested legal determinations for human review. A permissioned distributed ledger records only hashes, timestamps, procedural events, escrow states and execution proofs; personal data, communications, evidence and AI processing remain off-chain. Smart contracts are used as bounded enforcement tools for registration, escrow and execution of validated settlement terms, rather than as autonomous adjudicators. The article applies the architecture to three illustrative scenarios: asset seizure and recovery, exchange failure and mass claims, and crypto scams involving cross-border fraud. It then evaluates the model against European requirements concerning artificial intelligence, crypto-asset services, data protection, procedural fairness, cybersecurity and accountability. The contribution is twofold. First, it advances the concept of access to remedies by design, under which comprehension, participation, contestability, evidentiary integrity and enforceability are embedded into the architecture of digital dispute resolution. Second, it provides a technically specified evaluation framework for future prototyping and empirical validation. The article does not claim measured improvements in accessibility or efficiency; rather, it identifies testable design requirements and performance indicators for subsequent pilots, user studies and regulatory sandboxes.

items.title: OPTIMASI KOMPETENSI PEDAGOGIK GURU VOKASI MELALUI WORKSHOP PENYUSUNAN BAHAN AJAR DIGITAL BERBASIS DEEP LEARNING DI SMK PGRI 1 JAKARTA
items.abstract: The advancement of technological disruption in the digital era necessitates fundamental transformations within vocational education, particularly regarding teachers' readiness to produce innovative and contextual learning materials. Preliminary observations at SMK PGRI 1 Jakarta revealed that only 13.33% of teachers had independently developed interactive digital teaching materials due to technological barriers and time constraints. This Community Service (PkM) initiative aimed to enhance teachers' digital pedagogical competencies through a structured workshop focusing on the development of digital learning materials grounded in a deep learning approach assisted by artificial intelligence (AI) tools. The execution methodology incorporated the Asset-Based Community Development (ABCD) framework synthesized with the procedural phases of the Plomp model, encompassing preliminary research, development/prototyping, and assessment phases. The intervention was conducted offline on June 13, 2026, involving 30 vocational teachers from four expertise concentrations. Data were collected using self-evaluations, expert reviews, one-to-one evaluations, small-group evaluations, and final portfolio assessments. The evaluation results demonstrated that the digital teaching modules achieved an expert validity score of 4.40 out of 5.00 (highly valid), a small-group practicality score of 4.43 out of 5.00 (highly practical), and 86.67% of teachers successfully generated functional digital materials fulfilling vocational curriculum standards. This program offers practical implications as a sustainable instructional mentoring model to cultivate an autonomous digital learning ecosystem in vocational schools. Berdasarkan studi pendahuluan di SMK PGRI 1 Jakarta, ditemukan bahwa hanya 13,33% guru yang pernah mengembangkan bahan ajar digital interaktif secara mandiri akibat kendala literasi teknologi dan keterbatasan waktu. Program Pengabdian kepada Masyarakat (PkM) ini bertujuan untuk meningkatkan kompetensi pedagogik digital guru melalui workshop terstruktur penyusunan bahan ajar digital berbasis pendekatan pembelajaran mendalam (deep learning) berbantuan perangkat kecerdasan buatan (artificial intelligence / AI). Metode pelaksanaan mengadopsi pendekatan Asset-Based Community Development (ABCD) yang dipadukan dengan siklus pengembangan model Plomp, meliputi fase pengkajian awal (preliminary research), fase perancangan (development or prototyping phase), dan fase penilaian (assessment phase). Kegiatan dilaksanakan secara luring pada tanggal 13 Juni 2026 yang diikuti oleh 30 orang guru kejuruan dari empat konsentrasi keahlian. Pengumpulan data dilakukan menggunakan teknik self-evaluation, expert review, one-to-one evaluation, small group evaluation, serta penilaian portofolio produk akhir. Hasil evaluasi menunjukkan bahwa modul bahan ajar digital yang dikembangkan memperoleh skor validitas ahli sebesar 4,40 dari skala 5,00 (kategori sangat valid), tingkat kepraktisan kelompok sebesar 4,43 dari skala 5,00 (kategori sangat praktis), dan sebanyak 86,67% guru berhasil memproduksi bahan ajar digital siap pakai yang memenuhi kriteria kelayakan kurikulum vokasi. Program ini berimplikasi sebagai model pendampingan instruksional berkelanjutan dalam membangun ekosistem digital mandiri di sekolah kejuruan.

items.title: Optimization of Go-Kart Weight Distribution for Improved Handling and Cornering Performance
items.abstract: A go-kart is a small, lightweight four-wheeled vehicle designed for recreational, educational and competitive driving. This project deals with the design and fabrication of a go-kart powered by an internal combustion (IC) engine. The main objective is to develop a simple, strong, economical and serviceable vehicle using commonly available mechanical components and workshop processes. The project covers the selection of the IC engine, chassis design, steering system, braking system, power transmission, wheels and tyres, accelerator and control mechanism. The frame is designed to support the engine, driver and other components while maintaining adequate rigidity and stability. The engine converts the chemical energy of fuel into mechanical power, which is transmitted to the driving axle through a suitable transmission arrangement. The methodology includes requirement identification, conceptual design, component selection, basic engineering calculations, CAD/drawing preparation, material procurement, fabrication, assembly and testing. The report also discusses important safety aspects such as braking performance, steering response, chain guarding, fastener tightening and driver protection. The project provides practical understanding of automobile engineering, IC engines, manufacturing processes, machine design, welding, power transmission and vehicle testing. The final design can be further improved by reducing weight, improving ergonomics, optimizing power transmission and introducing additional safety and instrumentation.

items.title: Organizational Ergonomics in Robotics
items.abstract: The chapter introduces the organizational dimension of ergonomics for robotics. Specifically, it introduces the foundations of organizational ergonomics and sociotechnical principles for effective work systems design and development. It then highlights key challenges involved in issues related to work, activities, and quality of life in robotic setups. In this realm, attitudes towards robots and automation play a major role in the adoption of new technologies and change management in organizations. These broad-scale changes are important to be recognized as they shape human–robot interaction in various work settings, ranging from smart manufacturing to defence. The chapter then addresses specific aspects of teamwork and the design of high-performance teams. These topics include team performance and well-being, human function allocation, shared situation awareness, and job roles, amongst other such topics that will be explored later in the book by subsequent chapters. This chapter supplements the previous chapters on physical and cognitive ergonomics, but it goes beyond these aspects to highlight the organizational basis required to develop robotics holistically.

items.title: OWLET: On-Policy Weighted Learning via Evidence Transfer for Video Large Language Model Post-Training
items.abstract: Post-training has become a key stage for eliciting reasoning capabilities in Video Large Language Models (Video-LLMs). Existing post-training methods mainly follow two paradigms: reinforcement learning (RL) and on-policy distillation (OPD). However, they do not fully exploit visual evidence for effective training. RL supervises the policy with a single trajectory-level reward, which is too coarse-grained for video reasoning: the same response-level advantage is applied to every generated token, disregarding that the tokens of a video response are grounded in the visual stream to very different degrees. OPD provides token-level supervision through output-distribution matching, but lacks direct supervision of the spatiotemporal representations that produce those outputs. We observe across extensive experiments that the same model reasons more accurately when its video view combines global temporal context with question-relevant details. Comparing the same student-generated response under this view and uniform sampling reveals changes in token likelihoods and internal representations, providing a training signal for evidence use. Building on this observation, we propose OWLET, an evidence-privileged RL method that derives training signals from a richer teacher view. This view couples uniform global context with question-conditioned local windows, providing visual evidence without requiring a larger model. To better exploit this privileged visual evidence, OWLET introduces (i) \textbf{evidence-aware credit redistribution}, which compares token likelihoods across the two views and redistributes positive response-level advantages according to their relative evidence support; and (ii) \textbf{spatiotemporal state alignment}, which aligns the two views' hidden states on verifier-accepted responses.
